#1883. Torino vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 14:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 14:23

Still leading the pack in Serie A, surprise Scudetto challengers Lazio will visit mid-table Torino on Saturday night.

Unbeaten since August, the Biancocelesti extended their lead last weekend, while Toro's winless streak reached four straight games.

Yet to taste defeat in the league, Lazio sit three points above reigning champions Inter and two clear of city rivals Roma after storming through their first dozen games.

Having begun Gennaro Gattuso's reign with a shock Coppa Italia loss to Mantova, the Biancocelesti have since gone up through the gears, only dropping four points in Serie A so far.

Victory this week would take them onto 11 wins from 13 games, and the last team to make such a fast start was Napoli in the 2022-23 campaign, when they ultimately went on to win the title.

Lazio's most recent success, against Lecce, featured goals from two of their star players this term, as Tijjani Noslin bagged a brace before Davide Frattesi capped things off with a cheeky chip from outside the box.

Ahead of next month's Derby della Capitale, in which top spot could well be at stake, fans may even be dreaming of a first Scudetto for 27 years.

However, Gattuso will not look any further than Saturday's trip north to Turin, where Lazio have won half of their last 22 Serie A games against Torino.

That said, the capital club did not prevail when they last met in March, as Torino won 2-0 at Stadio Olimpico Grande.

So, the hosts can now seek back-to-back victories over Lazio for the first time since 2013, even if current form suggests they may fail.

While their Roman rivals are flying high, Toro have endured an uneven season under new boss Ignazio Abate: following a slow start, they then posted three consecutive wins, before slipping back down the table.

After last week's 1-0 loss to Napoli, Abate's side have picked up just one point from their last four matches, leaving them closer to the drop zone than Italy's top six.

While leaving Naples with anything is always a tough task, they cannot expect to thrive when they return to Turin.

Not only have the Granata conceded an average of nearly two goals per game there this season, but they are also on a record run of 11 Serie A home games without a clean sheet.

With only the league to consider, Gattuso has generally stuck to a similar Lazio lineup, but he is currently missing two regular starters.

Though defensive duo Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo are both sidelined with flexor injuries, captain Mattia Zaccagni has resumed full training and could be named on the bench.

While Frattesi is the visitors' top scorer with five Serie A goals, Noslin has notched at least one goal involvement in all of his last four matches.

Torino have been less potent this term, but Che Adams has four top-flight strikes and Giovanni Simeone must love playing his father's old club - the Argentinian has previously scored 10 league goals against Lazio.

Ardian Ismajli limped out of the loss to Napoli with an adductor injury and has subsequently undergone surgery, while Abate has fitness doubts about wing-backs Rafik Belghali and Ricardo Rodriguez.

As Belghali is still suffering with knee inflammation, Zakaria Aboukhlal, Nicolo Fortini or even Nathan Patterson could fill in on the hosts' right flank.

Perri; Comuzzo, Coco, Comert; Aboukhlal, Braganca, Mandragora, Vlasic, Cacciamani; Adams, Simeone

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Well acquainted from their Milan days, Gattuso and Abate will be foes for 90 minutes this weekend, when Lazio should continue their long unbeaten run.

As Torino struggle to keep clean sheets, the league leaders are sure to score, and they have conceded under one goal per game so far this term.

#1880. Sheepish Man United stars roll into Carrington after 4-0 trouncing at Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino and Co launch FA appeal against Leny Yoro's 'painful' red card

By OLLIE LEWIS, SPORTS DIGITAL EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER

Published: 05:58 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:41 EST, 23 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino hauled his beleaguered Man United stars back into Carrington early on Monday morning after the new manager's chastening Anfield bow on Sunday.

Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week, was served a sobering reality check at the hands of United's fierce rivals Liverpool, with the Red Devils on the receiving end of a 4-0 trouncing on Merseyside.

The Argentine bemoaned the impact of what he described as a harsh red card against defender Leny Yoro in the opening eight minutes of the contest, but admitted he has plenty to do to turn things around - with United stuck in 19th in the Premier League table.

And Pochettino had his players check in for training early on Monday morning, with a downcast Bruno Fernandes and his team-mates spotted arriving at around 8.30am - roughly an hour earlier than under Carrick.

Under Carrick's stewardship, players were given the day after a game off, and it remains to be seen whether Pochettino will do away with that approach in favour of a recovery day at the club's training ground - a similar approach to that taken by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

Man United stars were ordered back into training on Monday after their trouncing at Anfield

Matthijs de Ligt cut a contemplative figure as he drove through the gates at Carrington

Director of football Jason Wilcox continues to have questions to answer after Man United were unable to elevate themselves out of the relegation zone

News also came on Monday that Man United are appealing to the FA over Yoro’s controversial red card.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free kick as 10-man United were thrashed 4-0.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

In September, Pro Ref boss Howard Webb apologised to United when Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand after VAR incorrectly ruled that teammate Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play as he tried to head the ball in an offside position.

Last season, Webb acknowledged that the match officials got it wrong when they decided not to send off Brentford captain Nathan Collins for hauling back Bryan Mbeumo inside the box as United lost 3-1 at the Gtech Community Stadium.

New United head coach Pochettino blamed Yoro’s red card for the heavy defeat in his first game in charge, and was unhappy that Barrott took no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty area moments earlier.

'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the plan was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'

But more critical were former Red Devils Roy Keane and Gary Neville, both of whom were pushed to extremes assessing the match after the final whistle.

Lisandro Martinez was among the Man United defenders that Gary Neville did not feel were up to the task at Anfield

But incoming manager Pochettino was keen to place the majority of blame on the harsh red card doled out to Leny Yoro

Neville was driven to slapping his face in the Sky Sports studio to demonstrate Man United's defenders' lack of hunger and poise.

'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', he said before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'

The Overlap broadcaster slapped himself a number of times while repeating 'wake up!' and adding: 'You play for Man United'.

Keane was pushed to the brink of swearing in his snap description of the team's performance, adding that he thought Neville's verdict - that the 4-0 scoreline might have been worse under the circumstances - took players off the hook.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'

#1878. Brighton’s Conference League qualification path explained - How many points are needed after Craiova win?

Brighton still require six more points to guarantee their place in the last 16 of the Uefa Conference League following Thursday night's impressive 4-0 victory over Romanian league leaders Craiova.

Fabian Hurzeler's side are currently second in the league phase table - behind leaders Monaco - with 10 points from their opening four matches, putting them in a strong position to secure automatic qualification for the knockout stages.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The top eight teams qualify directly for the last 16, while those finishing between ninth and 24th must negotiate an additional knockout play-off round.

Brighton have two league-phase fixtures remaining, starting with a home meeting against leaders Monaco on December 10 before travelling to face Panathinaikos on December 17.

Winning both matches would take the Seagulls to 16 points and guarantee a top-eight finish, regardless of results elsewhere.

Four points from the remaining games would leave them on 14 and extremely well placed, although mathematical qualification would not be certain.

Three points would see them to 13 points and would still have a strong chance, depending on other results.

Hurzeler will be particularly encouraged by Brighton's defensive record, with the Seagulls yet to concede a goal in their four Conference League matches.

The Albion have scored nine times and will now look to finish the league phase strongly and avoid the extra play-off round in February.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler was delighted with the performance against Craiova

The German said: “I think that was a really good start, and also very important to make the game look easy, because especially the first goal helped us force [the opponent] to open up the space,” he said.

“That meant we could have more space to combine and more opportunity to attack their box. So I think we were very professional with good standards in the first half. Then, of course, the red card definitely helped us to finish - or to change - the structure of the game.

“In the second half we created plenty of chances. I wasn't happy that we weren't clinical and clean enough finishing these chances, because I think we dropped our level a little bit there. Overall, though, winning 4–0 means that we did a lot of things well.”

Here are the key dates for the 2026/27 UEFA Conference League knockout stages, should Brighton progress:

- Knockout play-off round: February 18 and 25, 2027.

- Final: June 2, 2027 – Beşiktaş Stadium, Istanbul, Turkey.

#1877. Rangers vs Falkirk - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 14:21

The Scottish Premiership's second and third-placed sides will meet on Saturday, when Rangers welcome Falkirk to Ibrox Stadium.

The hosts are second in the Scottish Premiership standings with 33 points, one point behind leaders Celtic, while the visitors are third with 24 points from 14 matches.

Rangers head into Saturday's match with their sights set on moving to the top of the Scottish Premiership standings for the first time this season.

The Gers trail leaders Celtic by just one point, meaning a victory would lift them above their Old Firm rivals, at least until the Bhoys take on Hearts on Sunday afternoon.

Derek McInnes' men will be full of confidence of claiming all three points, with Rangers heading into the matchday 15 fixture enjoying a sensational 14-game unbeaten run across all competitions.

In the league, Rangers have won 10 and drawn two matches during that run, including winning each of their last three Scottish Premiership fixtures, beating St Mirren 2-0, Motherwell 2-1 and Aberdeen 3-2.

The Gers are also looking to extend their superb record at Ibrox, having won all of their last nine home games, scoring 22 and conceding just four goals in that time.

Despite their fantastic form coming into this match, Rangers will expect a tough test against visitors Falkirk, who travel to Ibrox off the back of six consecutive league triumphs.

That run includes particularly notable wins against Celtic (2-0) and Hearts (5-2), and the Bairns will now be looking to add Rangers' scalp to their collection.

Thanks to those six victories, Falkirk have rapidly ascended to third in the Scottish Premiership standings with 24 points from 14 matches, although they only lead Hearts - who have played one game fewer - by one point.

Alongside their impressive recent run, Falkirk will draw further self belief from their formidable record on the road this season, recording three wins, three draws and suffering just one loss away from home in the league.

John McGlynn's side have, however, failed to defeat Rangers in any of their last seven encounters, including a 2-1 defeat earlier this season.

Rangers are set to be without Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Jose Cifuentes, Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti due to ongoing injuries, while Ross McCrorie is also a doubt with a hamstring injury.

Ryan Don Naderi is Rangers' top scorer in the league with seven goals, and the forward should continue just behind Kevin Kelsy in the forward line.

Falkirk are also contending with several injury absences, including Aidan Nesbitt, Aodhan Doherty, Brad Spencer, Leon McCann and Ryan Strain, while Ethan Laidlaw is a doubt to feature.

Jacob Murrell is Falkirk's top scorer with eight league goals, including seven in his last seven appearances, and the forward will start just ahead of Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames in attack.

Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Bouanani, Naderi, Gassama; Kelsy

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Krauhaus, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell

Both teams head into this match in fantastic form, leading us to expect a hard-fought encounter. However, given Rangers' formidable Ibrox form and their recent upperhand in this fixture, we are predicting a victory for the hosts.

#1876. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1875. Celtic defend head of security amid fan group tensions

Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared that four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.

A statement from the ultras group stated the four had been “finally cleared of wrongdoing” over the incident, which took place during a game against Falkirk on October 25 last year.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The group accused Celtic of “smearing” them with their statement on November 7 last year, which outlined an indefinite ban on about 250 supporters that eventually lasted nearly six months.

Celtic had written that about 100 Green Brigade members took part in an “orchestrated” attempt to prevent an individual being arrested following an incident with a steward and that the large group “verbally abused and assaulted the steward and police officers”.

A Green Brigade statement read: “Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.

“The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed.”

The group called for Celtic to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with the club’s head of security, Mark Hargreaves, at last year’s abandoned annual general meeting.

“This week’s outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year,” they added.

“It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves’ subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives.

“We maintain that Mark Hargreaves has introduced a poisonous security culture to Celtic Park and does not hold the trust of supporters whose safety he is supposed to be responsible for. His position is untenable.”

Celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.

A statement added: “The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable – it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.

“Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council.”

Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a “campaign of personal harassment and abuse” towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.

They added: “Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.

“Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action.”

#1874. Real Madrid vs Alaves - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:20

Real Madrid will be aiming to make it 11 straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last nine games against Alaves, including a 2-1 victory in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign.

Real Madrid will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League, with that success making it 10 victories in a row in all competitions.

Jose Mourinho's side are flying, with their winning run including six in Spain's top flight, and they are currently second in the La Liga table, only three points off the leaders Barcelona.

Los Blancos now have three straight league matches against Alaves, Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao before resuming their Champions League campaign away to Arsenal on December 9.

Real Madrid would go level on points with Barcelona should they manage to win this match, and they have been victorious in 38 of their previous 46 games against Alaves in all competitions, suffering only five defeats in the process.

Vinicius Junior is still finding it difficult to show his best form for Real Madrid, but Kylian Mbappe is having another incredible campaign, netting 19 times in 18 appearances in all competitions.

Alaves will be the huge underdogs this weekend, but two of their last three wins over Real Madrid have come away from home, including a 2-1 success at Bernabeu in November 2020.

The Blue and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Deportivo La Coruna, with the result leaving them in ninth spot in the La Liga table on 16 points, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and five defeats from their 13 matches.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have been excellent at home this season, picking up 13 points from seven matches, but they are still waiting for their first away success of the campaign.

Alaves finished 14th in Spain's top flight last season, only one point above the relegation zone, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27.

The Basque outfit will be the fresher of the two teams following Real Madrid's Champions League involvement, but they will be up against a side that have the second-best defensive record (11 conceded) and second-best attacking record (33 scored) during the current season.

Real Madrid will be missing Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg), Ferland Mendy (hip) and Endrick (groin) through injury on Saturday, but no fresh issues have been reported.

There will be changes to the side that took to the field for the first whistle against PSV, with Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen potentially all being introduced into the defence.

Jude Bellingham should also return to the starting side, with Yan Diomande potentially being rested from the first whistle to allow Arda Guler and Vinicius Junior to feature in the wide areas.

As for Alaves, Facundo Garces (knee), Mikel Rodriguez (knee) and Hugo Noava (muscle) are unavailable.

Given the nature of the result and indeed the performance against Deportivo last time out, it is possible that it could be same again in terms of the starting team for the visitors.

Lucas Boye has scored six times in 12 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set to feature in the final third, while Denis Suarez and Antonio Blanco are also set to be in the XI.

Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Tchouameni; Guler, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe

Sivera; Tenaglia, Koski, Otto; Perez, Ibanez, Blanco, Suarez, Rebbach; Martinez, Boye

Alaves deserve credit for what has been a solid season to date, but Real Madrid are in a good place at the moment, and we are fully expecting Mourinho's side to claim another three points.

#1873. Fabian Hürzeler gives brilliant answer to Gary Lineker's Brighton title race theory

Gary Lineker argued that the Seagulls could become genuine title contenders – and be ‘very difficult to stop’ – if they had a striker in the mould of former Leicester City forward Jamie Vardy.

All-time leading Premier League goalscorer Alan Shearer agreed but also praised the quality of recent performances, including the surprise defeat at Hull City.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Hürzeler insists he is happy with the attacking options already at his disposal, pointing to Brighton’s goalscoring record and the number of players capable of finding the net. Albion lead the Premier League goals scored table, finding the net 26 times in 11 games.

Asked about Lineker and Shearer’s praise for Brighton as one of the most entertaining teams in the league, Hürzeler welcomed the recognition but stressed that performances, rather than outside opinion, must remain the priority.

“If they say this, of course we should listen to it,” he said.

“On the other side, being the best football team doesn't mean you automatically win games.

“We really have to keep focusing on our performances, that’s what we can control. We can't control what others think about us.

“We can only control how well we prepare for a game and how high our levels are on matchday.

“The truth is always on the pitch, and therefore we have to get back to our highest level.”

Hürzeler was more emphatic when asked whether he agreed with Lineker’s suggestion that Brighton were missing a clinical, traditional centre-forward.

“An Alan Shearer?” the German replied, tongue-in-cheek.

“No, no. I think we have a lot of good strikers. When you look at how many goals we've scored in the season so far, and how many goals we scored today.

"We might not have one striker but we have plenty of players who are able to score goals.

“That's what has made us strong in the past and what will make us strong in the future, hopefully on Sunday as well.”

The Brighton head coach was speaking after his side responded to their disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City with a 4-0 victory over Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Next up is a home match against Newcastle United, in the Premier League, this weekend.

Hürzeler specifically named the attacking players he believes can provide the goals, making clear that he has no concerns about the options available to him.

He added: “We're very happy with Kostoulas. We're very happy with [Georginio] Rutter.

"We're also happy with Tobi [Promise David], who came onto the pitch today against Craiova.”

The head coach also appeared keen to ensure that the defeat at Hull did not define the assessment of his team's attacking play.

Brighton created opportunities at the MKM Stadium but were unable to find a way past an inspired goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis, prompting Lineker to suggest that a striker with Vardy's instincts could make them much harder to stop.

Hürzeler, however, would rather focus on the wider picture than one frustrating afternoon in front of goal.

“We're focusing on the positives,” he said.

"We are not focusing on one game where we missed a few chances.”

The 4-0 victory over Craiova offered an immediate reminder of Brighton's goalscoring capabilities, although Hürzeler will now want his players to carry that performance into Sunday's match.

#1872. When St Johnstone’s owner was offered square go by Rangers boss - and the call players still wind him up about

The amount of health and safety regulations required in the construction business nowadays means Geoff Brown is happy to be free the daily responsibility of running the family firm he established.

However, some form of welfare protection might have been helpful at the moment he saw Graeme Souness storming down the corridor towards him. “He was threatening to knock my block off,” he recalls.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

St Johnstone tea-lady Aggie Moffat had erupted because of the state in which Rangers had left the away dressing-room following a 1-1 draw in February 1991. She made sure Souness knew all about it. Brown was in the boardroom with the directors of both clubs when they heard a “serious commotion” in the foyer. The chairman went outside and was met by Souness, who ‘offered’ to take him outside.

“I did not make a noise of it at the time,” says Brown, who wonders what impact it might have had on Souness’ career had he agreed to take part in the square go the Ibrox manager was suggesting. “David Murray phoned me the following week to thank me for not making a noise about what happened,” he says.

Ownership of St Johnstone – his 38 years at the helm of the club is the longest any individual has owned a professional football club in Scotland in modern times – has afforded Brown, now 83, a ringside seat and very nearly active involvement in so many of the colourful incidents characterising the game in this country.

The Aggie incident is certainly included among those. Despite Brown keeping schtum about the threat from Souness at the time, it’s become one of Scottish football’s most well-rehearsed anecdotes.

Rightly so, because the so-called storm in a teacup had profound repercussions. Souness ended up citing the incident as one of the reasons he left Rangers for Liverpool shortly afterwards. Brown, by contrast, has not roamed far. Building houses for others occupied his time. After that proved profitable, it permitted him the luxury of time to devote to saving St Johnstone from the clutches of the receivers.

This was in 1986. The Perth club “were the strongest team in the country”. In other words, they were holding the rest of Scottish football up and were sitting plum last in the pile. One afternoon, shortly after Brown had agreed to take on all the debt, Tayside Safety Committee paid a visit. “There were about ten of them,” he recalls. “And they were put in the boardroom. I said: ‘I am sorry, what are you doing here?’

“One replied: ‘We are here to close down the club’. Notices had been given to the previous board that had never been passed on to us. They hadn’t met any of the safety standards at the last inspection, and nothing had been done after the inspections. So they were there to close the club down.”

Forty years and three major trophies later, Brown can reflect with a degree of satisfaction on his impact on football in his local area. But when he was presented with an Outstanding Contribution Award by first minister John Swinney at the Courier Business awards night in Dundee as recently as October, it was more his success as a housebuilder – he set up GS Brown Construction in 1970 – and charitable work that were being recognised.

As Brown was making his way in the construction business, he and his young family lived in a council house in Tulloch. It looked on to berry fields, owned by a farmer called Bruce McDiarmid.

Around twenty years later, as the new owner of St Johnstone FC, he met McDiarmid to negotiate a land deal. The trouble was, St Johnstone had no money to buy the fields on which it was being proposed they could build a new stadium. Asda’s interest in buying their then stadium, Muirton Park, came to light shortly afterwards.

Brown offered McDiarmid a 20 per cent stake in the club for the land, a deal the farmer’s lawyer advised him to reject. But McDiarmid accepted it. When Asda later offered £5 million for the Muirton Park site Brown cannily persuaded the supermarket firm to cover the cost of the new stadium instead. Some might still be under the impression, incorrect as it turns out, that McDiarmid gifted the land to St Johnstone, perhaps with the sole condition that they had to name the stadium after him.

“He certainly did not,” says Brown. “One way or the other, it did take a bit of persuading. I went with him to see his lawyer, who was older than Bruce. ‘No,’ the lawyer said. ‘You don’t really want that. If you are going to sell it, sell it’. Within a year I had Asda going to give us £5 million for Muirton Park. If you are sitting with 20 per cent of that you are not doing too bad…”

Brown’s new book is called Building My Life – shades of Alex Ferguson’s Managing My Life – but it could be called The Art of the Deal. It includes lots of wrangling and horse-trading, sometimes involving actual horses (As well as football, Brown is also a renowned racehorse owner). He doesn’t always come out on the right side of such negotiations, such as when the players were negotiating bonuses at the start of the 1998-99 season.

“That was a disaster,” he says. “The players – Paul Kane, Roddy Grant, Allan Preston – they were at (managing director) Stewart Duff because you always agree the bonuses at the start of the year. They are sitting arguing about bonuses for each potential position. And they come to 4th place. ‘4th place – are you happy with £250,000?’ Stewart asked. ‘Aye, go on then,’ I told him. ‘Now they are asking me for third place,’ he says.

“I said: ‘Stewart, they will never get third’. He says: ‘I agree with you. So should we just give them half a million?’”

Reader, they got third place, qualifying for the Uefa Cup in the process. “To this day the ones like Preston and Kane keep rubbing it in,” Brown says. “They tell me: ‘The one thing you got wrong with St Johnstone is that day you gave us too much money!’

“At that time, European football meant you ran at a loss. Because you’re hiring planes in the holiday period. Chartering a plane was expensive. Plus the (bonus) money we were paying players.”

Not that Brown regrets any of it. “It’s what you’re in it for, isn’t it?” he says. Now out of it after selling his majority stake in the club to Atlanta-based lawyer Adam Webb, he can enjoy attending games such as this weekend’s Tayside derby against Dundee United at Tannadice. At home games he sits in the Geoff Brown Stand. “The best bit is, whatever the scoreline, I can sleep afterwards,” he says.

Stewardship of a football club can take a toll, clearly. But Brown made some good friends, none better than Paul Sturrock. Of all the managers he employed, he was the one with whom he shared the closest relationship, to the extent that Brown’s wife Joyce regarded him as one of the family. “He’d let himself into the house and put the kettle on,” recalls Brown.

Even adversaries were entertained, such as Ron Dixon. The colourful one-time owner of Dundee actually bought Brown’s family home in St Madoes for those rare times when he was in Scotland. The Canadian complained to the St Johnstone owner that he’d been sold a pup when buying the Dens Park club. “They told me I was getting a sleeping giant!” he lamented. Brown told Sturrock. “Aye, they’re all lying in the cemetery!” the former Dundee United winger replied.

Memo to Dundonians of either hue: Brown has a few arch things to say about Dundee natives. However, citizens of the fair city of Perth will enjoy Brown’s book, likewise anyone partial to a classic rags-to-riches tale.

Building My Life: The Geoff Brown Story will be launched in the Centenary Suite at McDiarmid Park on November 30, from 6pm until 8pm. The book will be available in the St Johnstone club shop in Perth City Centre and at McDiarmid Park on match days.

#1871. Brighton injury latest: Fabian Hurzeler issues Kaoru Mitoma update ahead of Newcastle

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW

Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger)

The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25

'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'

Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

'It's devastating,' said Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just said to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'

Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'

Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway said on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'

Given what the Reds are currently experiencing, that magnificent promotion campaign must seem like a world away.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The pair are now fighting fires at the wrong end of League One; beleaguered Barnsley currently prop up the table following a wretched 11-match winless streak.

In his second coming at Oakwell, Stendel named McGeehan, a player he rates and trusts, as his on-pitch leader in the summer.

So far this term, the Reds chief has largely been spared the ire of increasingly agitated followers; most have elected to vent their frustration toward the Oakwell hierarchy instead.

But given Barnsley's atrocious autumnal numbers - two points taken from the last available 33 - chatter is also starting to centre on the German's position.

For McGeehan, the club's top-scorer with nine goals, it provides a personal element in his quest to help the stricken Reds change the narrative of a hard season.

He also shares sympathy with Stendel, given Barnsley's tendencies to continually shoot themselves in the foot - which he feels has nothing to do with the head coach.

A case in point was at Bradford City on Tuesday, when all three of the visitors' concessions were self-inflicted.

Speaking ahead of the crunch trip to fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, McGeehan said: "I think coming in after the game, a lot of the boys were saying: 'the gaffer's going to be pulling his hair out' because that was just down to the players' mistakes.

"And it's happened too many times this season, we've made poor individual errors that have led to goals and caused us to lose games we probably shouldn't have.

"We want to get a positive result for everyone at the club.

"But obviously the gaffer's someone I've worked with before and you can see it completely consumes him. He wants the very best and he's passionate to get Barnsley into a good place, as we all are. We're all fighting together.

"It can all change very quickly. But it starts with us on the pitch getting a positive result. This poor run's lasted way too long and we've got to draw a line in the sand.

"Obviously, there's a lot of positive things that we've done in games and it's just trying to get that game where it clicks and then you go from there."

The busy run to the turn of the year looks critical for Barnsley, currently four points adrift of safety, with several fixtures coming up against sides around them.

Should the Reds manage to chip away with some much-needed wins, January will come into sharp focus.

Recruiting a defensive lieutenant and an experienced leader of the line are surely two huge priorities for a side that is currently dangerously weak in both boxes, where games are decided, despite getting other things right elsewhere.

On the importance of bringing in some seniority in the new year at the sharp ends of the pitch, McGeehan observed: "Potentially. You can look at that obviously when you're not doing well, you sort of start to pick apart different things.

"At the start of the season, when we started quite well, you sort of think: 'oh, we've got a youthful, energetic side'.

"There's always two ways you can spin it. I've seen experienced players make mistakes for goals and be short of confidence as well. January will come and teams always make signings but all we are concentrating on is now and do what we can with what we've got.

"We've got some really good players here and hopefully we can turn the corner. It's everyone sticking together and trying to fight. It's the only way out of this."

McGeehan admits that listening to opposing managers and pundits continuing to label Barnsley as a good footballing side is becoming 'boring'.

For his part, Stendel concurs, adding: "This is easy to say when you win the game and keep the points. I don't like it."

The Reds boss also has no truck with the disquiet of supporters either.

It spilled over at the final whistle at Valley Parade on Tuesday with chants of 'You're not fit to wear the shirt' aimed at players.

The Oakwell boss, who confirmed that Reyes Cleary is not yet back in training, with Cieran Slicker and Makenzie Kirk having issues ahead of the weekend, added: "When you are upset, you say things like that. This is not different at Barnsley to other clubs in the world.

"I also have to support and protect my team. They are trying to do their best. It is not enough at the moment for the expectation of what we have as a club and also not for the supporters."

#1866. Stockport County vs Leyton Orient - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 15:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:05

Looking to remain top of the League One table heading into the final month of the year, Stockport County welcome Leyton Orient to Edgeley Park on Saturday afternoon.

The Hatters currently hold a three-point lead at the summit after recording their third consecutive victory with a 3-0 win away to Cambridge United, while the O's are hoping to close the gap on the playoff places after beating AFC Wimbledon 4-1 last time out.

Following their agonisingly narrow failure to secure promotion to the Championship last season, Stockport County parted ways with long-serving manager Dave Challinor and appointed former Rochdale boss Jimmy McNulty as his replacement.

McNulty has so far overseen 21 matches in charge of the Hatters across all competitions, recording 13 wins, four draws and four defeats to give him an impressive win rate of 61.9%.

Ten of those victories have come in League One, with Stockport looking to enter December at the top of the table after collecting 32 points from their opening 16 matches, a lead they could extend to six points if results elsewhere go their way and they secure a fourth consecutive league win.

Their impressive league form has also carried over into the cup competitions, with McNulty's men finishing top of their EFL Trophy group and booking their place in the next round of the FA Cup, although they survived a major scare earlier this month, coming from two goals behind to beat Isthmian League side Cray Wanderers 3-2.

More recently, the Greater Manchester outfit climbed to the summit of League One with an emphatic 3-0 victory over Cambridge, a match that featured a superb free-kick from captain Oliver Norwood.

The three goals scored last weekend took Stockport's league tally to 32 for the season, a total bettered by no other side in the third tier and only three teams across England's top four divisions.

As for visitors Leyton Orient, they have enjoyed a more consistent campaign this time around after spending much of the 2025-26 season battling near the bottom of the table and ultimately finishing just one place above the relegation zone.

After their opening 14 League One matches, the London-based side sit 12th under the continued leadership of Richie Wellens, who recently surpassed 250 games in charge of the O's, with six wins, two draws and six defeats leaving them on 20 points.

Although victory on Saturday, at a ground where Stockport boast the best home record in the division, would not be enough to lift Orient into the playoff places, it could leave them just three points outside the top six, with games in hand over all but one of the teams currently above them.

The O's most recently continued their impressive home form with a convincing 4-1 victory over London neighbours AFC Wimbledon, securing their fourth league win in their last five matches at Brisbane Road.

In fact, Wellens' side are already closing in on surpassing their total number of home victories from the whole of last season, having won half of their league fixtures on home soil so far in 2026-27.

Although the two sides finished at opposite ends of the table last season, neither could claim bragging rights in their meetings, with both encounters ending in draws.

The last time either side won this fixture within 90 minutes was in February 2025, the same season they faced each other in the League One playoff semi-finals.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Hoping to make it six consecutive victories in all competitions, McNulty will be keen to stick with his winning formula and has the option to do so after his side came through their latest fixture without any fresh injury concerns.

Norwood is expected to retain his place in midfield, while club top scorer Kyle Wootton will lead the line as he looks to add to his 10 League One goals this season, with Jack Diamond operating out wide.

Leyton Orient also look set to travel from the capital with the option of naming an unchanged starting XI following last weekend's victory.

Former Tottenham Hotspur forward Dane Scarlett is expected to lead the line again after scoring in consecutive matches, while Alex Gilbert should retain his place in midfield after scoring and providing an assist against Wimbledon.

Wellens will, however, remain without Ollie O'Neill, who is expected to miss four months after undergoing surgery shortly after returning from a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare are also expected to remain in the treatment room.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Gordon, O'Connell, Pye; Glover, Bate, Norwood, Ennis; Diamond, Wootton, Wood

Baxter; Stevens, Gilchrist, Edmonds-Green, Boniface; El Mizouni, Gilbert; Connolly, C. Wellens, Dobra; Scarlett

Although Leyton Orient have produced some encouraging results in recent weeks, we expect the league leaders to show why they sit at the top of the table and maintain their push for promotion.

We see Stockport having enough quality to extend their impressive home record and make it four consecutive league victories.

#1862. Silly Leeds United punishment shows Daniel Farke's serious approach to complacency

Earlier in the season, the German manager told The Yorkshire Post of his – slightly tongue in cheek – horror at Ao Tanaka wearing gloves in training before the weather had turned cold, and this week he gave a member of staff a dressing down to try and keep his squad grounded after Saturday's hugely impressive 4-1 win at Chelsea.

Both the "crime" and the punishment were light-hearted but with a serious message about complacency, and it is a balance Farke always looks to strike.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Leeds are in seventh in the Premier League and have consistently been around the likely positions to qualify for Europe this season, but Farke has always taken a two-pronged attitude towards expectations, encouraging supporters to get ahead of themselves but not those who work for him.

"What I can guarantee is I will make sure that no one here at the training ground at Thorp Arch is too big time and I'm not one per cent concerned about my players," he said when the topic of Europe was raised ahead of Saturday's Premier League visit from newly-promoted Coventry City.

"We had a staff member this week who came out after a great win against Chelsea more or less celebrating in the first session.

"I know it's a bit colder right now and you have to put yourself into warm clothes but instead of wearing a hat (for training) – a hat is totally fine – he was wearing a snood over his head like a 20-year-old creative No 10 who enjoys himself.

"It was as if he had won the game at Chelsea all alone.

"It was a long working day for him, I made sure. He was treating our kit men and from now on he stays in shorts and T-shirts until the end of January on the outside pitches.

"I don't allow anyone to be big time, not one staff member, not one player. We know exactly what we're coming from and if anyone thinks we are too good for this and can be cool like a 20-year-old No 10, one of my staff members, I will make sure that everyone is back to work and doesn't enjoy himself too much.

"We have not achieved 38 points so far (his mark for avoiding relegation), so there's no reason to lean back, just enjoy and stop working.

"It's good to be already on 17 points at this stage (11 games in). It's definitely a good amount and gives us confidence and belief in what you're doing.

"But at this level the momentum can change quickly and for that we won't allow ourselves to be too big time or to enjoy ourselves too much.

"We are in a good mood at the moment and we work, train and play with confidence but nothing else.

"The Premier League is the best league in the world. We can only win points if we are 100 per cent on it."

A silly response to a seemingly trivial offence (with a much more serious underlying issue) is a balance Farke is conscious of striking.

"It's perhaps not typical for a German fella to have a good sense of humour – at least that's a bit the reputation – but I think in general everyone is at his best in every job when you feel valued, when you feel comfortable when you do your job with confidence and this is also what we try to create," commented Farke.

"I've seen some statistics that we were the hardest-working side over the last (Premier League) weekend. At Chelsea we covered more distance and high-speed intensity runs than any other team at Premier League level.

"This is one side of how we work really hard with focused, concentrated work but we always want to do this with a smile on our face.

"We want to make sure that everyone enjoys coming to work and it's not just hoping for the next day off so I don't see the manager, the staff member or assistant coach.

"Sometimes you have to give them a day off but we also want to create an atmosphere where everyone feels safe and is allowed to make a joke and also joke at my costs.

"You also give the sign that you know how important and how serious football is but it's never more important than the human being.

"When I name the squad on Friday there are some tough decisions and top players won't make it. When I name the starting line-up it's tough for them but then we have to make sure that we have something to cheer and to laugh about.

"Hopefully the most important thing is success and winning points but also to have a good atmosphere.

"I hope my jokes are not too old-school for the players because I'm getting older and older."

Meanwhile, striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract until the end of 2028-29, by when he will have just turned 32.

#1860. Scott Lindsey embraces York City expectations as he targets more than League Two consolidation

The Minstermen, who ended their 10-year exile from the Football League last season, sit fifth ahead of Saturday's trip to Colchester United, raising hopes of successive promotions.

Lindsey is embracing that pressure at a club that have made no secret of their ambition to go back-to-back.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"The only pressure I've got is from myself because I know what this group is capable of," said the York boss. "I put pressure on myself to do well and believe that we're good enough to have a really good season.

"I haven't got any pressure from anywhere else. It's a football club that want to get somewhere really quickly, which suits me as well.

"I'm ambitious. I don't want to just make the numbers up and finish mid-table. It would be a bit of a waste of a season, even though that would be seen as success to a lot of people.

"It's our first season in the division for 10 years and I want to do really well."

York have lost just four of their 16 games, bouncing back from consecutive defeats to claim their first win on the road at Rochdale before sharing the spoils with fellow promotion hopefuls Walsall.

City also have an FA Cup tie against Carlisle to look forward to for a place in the third round.

"I think we're in a really good position in the division," added Lindsey.

"The football club hasn't been in this league for 10 years. To say we are where we are in the division and into the second round of the FA Cup, I see that as a massive positive.

"I'm over the moon with the start that we've had."

Rather than making wholesale changes when he arrived in the summer, Lindsey has sought to build on the winning culture he inherited.

Maintaining the momentum generated in the National League was an important consideration as York made the step up to League Two, with the new manager recognising the value of what was already in place.

"Definitely," said Lindsey, whose side are just one point adrift of the automatic promotion places.

"The club before I turned up was a winning machine anyway, which is why I didn't change loads straight away. I didn't feel I had to because I thought there was a lot of good work done here.

"I just wanted to put my stamp on it, which I feel I've done, and the lads have taken on that information and executed it brilliantly.

"It's a strange situation because when you come into a club as a manager, you're normally coming into a bit of a mess. But I wasn't; I was coming into a real structured team who were used to winning. I had to sit into that.

"My style isn't too dissimilar to what was happening before. There are little tweaks where I feel I've made us a little bit more robust for this division. Over the years of me being here, it'll be more my team."
