#1832. Raheem Sterling dodges prison for dangerously driving Lamborghini

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

#1830. How England could line up without Harry Kane as Thomas Tuchel given unusual solution (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 16:00

England manager Thomas Tuchel has been told to consider an unusual solution to Harry Kane's injury absence if the Three Lions captain misses March's Nations League quarter-final with Norway.

Tuchel and co are sweating over the fitness of the Ballon d'Or winner after he was ruled out for a 'few months' with a serious ankle injury, sustained in Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln earlier this month.

Kane had to undergo surgery to correct the torn ligament, and there is a chance that he could now sit out the reunion with World Cup quarter-final foes Norway, whom the Three Lions face at the end of March 2027.

Tuchel has a plethora of alternative centre-forward options at his disposal, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Dominic Solanke, Ivan Toney, Ollie Watkins and Championship star Will Lankshear.

However, ex-England forward Brian Deane has exclusively told Sports Mole that Tuchel could instead consider using either Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers as a false nine rather than deploying a pure centre-forward.

“It is difficult because I do not think England have another centre-forward who can do exactly what Harry Kane does," Deane said. "He is not the quickest, but he is intelligent, drops into pockets and allows the team to rotate around him. He has earned the right for the manager to build that structure.

“Dominic Calvert-Lewin is very good at holding the ball up, bringing others into play and competing in the air. Whether he would score the same types of goals as Kane is another question.

“Solanke has the ability, but I am not convinced about his confidence at the moment. The England shirt can weigh heavily.

“Ivan Toney has a strong all-round game, is excellent in the box and is one of the best penalty-takers around. The question would be how he adjusts to the tempo of international football from the league he is playing in.

“Will Lankshear is perhaps a little inexperienced. Bringing him into the squad is one thing; asking him to lead the line ahead of those other players is another.

“Tuchel might decide not to use a conventional centre-forward. He could put Jude Bellingham or Morgan Rogers further forward and approach it differently. It is very difficult to replicate Kane. He has done amazingly well and is almost irreplaceable.”

According to data from Transfermarkt, Bellingham has only made one club appearance as an out-and-out centre-forward, compared to 23 for Rogers during his career.

If Deane's prediction comes true and Tuchel does opt for a false-nine approach, the Chelsea man should therefore be at the head of the queue for striking duties, especially having also featured in that role for the Blues already this season against Tottenham Hotspur.

Bellingham has licence to continue in the number 10 role as a result, and Rogers being moved centrally opens the door for a fit-again Bukayo Saka to reclaim his place on the right flank.

However, there is every chance that Kane will recover in time to face Norway, aiming to build on an unparalleled record of 93 goals in 127 matches for his country.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

#1826. Manchester United vs Brentford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 18:43

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match at Old Trafford as Manchester United head coach takes place on Saturday afternoon when Brentford visit the Theatre of Dreams for an intriguing Premier League contest.

While the Red Devils occupy a place in the relegation zone, sitting 19th in the Premier League table, the Bees are nine points and 13 places better off in sixth spot after 11 matches.

Chaos and drama seem to follow Man United wherever they go this season, as the Red Devils were involved in an action-packed 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday that saw them depart Portugal feeling aggrieved after a contest marred by contentious officiating.

Man United saw two goals chalked off in a match featuring three penalties and a late red card for Youri Tielemans. They were on course to claim victory via a quickfire Bruno Fernandes brace that overturned Luis Suarez's opening spot-kick, only for a Senne Lammens goalkeeping error to allow Suarez to salvage a share of the spoils for Sporting.

Pochettino was “so proud” of his players for how they handled “such a tough game” and believes that their performance was the “best medicine” to prepare for their next fixture in the Premier League, one they can ill-afford to drop points in if they wish to ease growing fears of relegation.

Two more goals conceded in Lisbon means Man United have shipped a total of 36 goals in 17 games across all competitions – more than any other side in Europe’s top-five leagues – while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in over 75 days (13 games) since a 4-0 UCL success over Sabah on September 10.

The Red Devils were put to the sword 4-0 by rivals Liverpool at Anfield in Pochettino’s first Premier League game in charge last weekend, leaving them second-bottom of the table with the fewest wins (one), second-most goals conceded (23) and on a nine-match winless streak in the top flight (D5 L4) – their longest such run since 1988-89.

Sitting just one point adrift of safety, Man United could climb out of the drop zone for the first time in three weeks with a victory over Brentford. The Red Devils have won only four of their last eight meetings with the Bees (D1 L3), but all four of those have come at Old Trafford, including a 2-1 success in April of last season.

Brentford travel to the red side of Manchester in buoyant mood after securing a comprehensive 4-0 home victory over Everton on Monday – their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League equalling their 4-0 thrashing of Man United in August 2022.

Keane Lewis-Potter – who extended his contract with the club this week – scored two deflected goals before the Toffees were reduced to 10 men. Vitaly Janelt and Fabio Carvalho were also on target to help the Bees ease to their second win in three games and move to within four points of the top four.

Keith Andrews lauded his team’s “outstanding” performance against Everton and he now heads into Saturday’s fixture seeking to address Brentford’s contrasting home and away form, with only four of their 17 points accumulated on the road this season (D4 L1).

Including results from last season, Brentford are enduring their longest winless away run in the Premier League (10 matches – D7 L3) and their longest winless run on the road in any division since a 15-game streak in the Championship between April and December 2018.

The Bees will be aiming to end an eight-game losing run at Old Trafford and claim their first-ever Premier League away victory over Man United this weekend, as they bid to boost their early-season European ambitions and consolidate their place in the top six.

Manchester United form (all competitions):

Man United are still having to cope without Carlos Baleba (hamstring), Benjamin Sesko (calf) and Manuel Ugarte (knee) due to injury, while Marcus Rashford (hip), Luke Shaw (fitness), Karl Darlow (knee) and Bruno Fernandes (illness) are all doubtful, the latter of whom missed training on Friday.

A potential return for Shaw - who has not played since October 10 - would likely see Lisandro Martinez either move back into the centre of defence or drop out of the side altogether, while Diogo Dalot is pushing to return at right-back at the expense of Noussair Mazraoui.

Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool has been overturned, allowing the youngster to start at centre-back alongside either Martinez, Harry Maguire of Matthijs De Ligt, who was handed a surprise first PL start in 357 days against Liverpool after a lengthy injury layoff.

Matheus Cunha is available to return from a European ban and will likely replace either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee. This would see former Brentford star Bryan Mbeumo either move back over to the right flank or start as a centre-forward.

As for Brentford, Igor Thiago is serving the second game of a three-match suspension, while Aaron Hickey (thigh), Nathan Collins (knee), Rico Henry (groin), Kaye Furo (ankle), Antoni Milambo and Josh Dasilva (both fitness) remain sidelined, the latter two are targeting a return before Christmas.

Mathias Jensen has scored more goals against Man United (four) than any other opponent in his career and the midfielder will be hoping to force his way back into the first XI at the expense of Mikkel Damsgaard.

Kevin Schade is another pushing for a recall in attack and could come in for either Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony, while Callum Wilson could retain his starting spot as the central striker – he has never scored at Old Trafford in seven previous visits in all competitions.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha; Zirkzee

Kelleher; Kayode, Van den Berg, Ajer, Lewis-Potter; Yarmoliuk, Janelt; Anthony, Jensen, Schade; Wilson

Despite Man United’s dismal start in the top flight, Pochettino's first Premier League home match in charge should spark enough attacking urgency from the hosts to trouble a Bees side that has struggled on its travels.

Taking into account that each of the last six head-to-head battles has seen both teams score, while 12 of Man United’s last 14 home matches have produced over 2.5 goals, we can envisage a wide-open, end-to-end affair ending all square on this occasion.

#1823. Frick promises his Dons will maintain their positive approach and go on the attack in Ibrox clash

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 13:41 EST, 23 November 2026

Aberdeen  boss Mario Frick has vowed to go on the attack when his new-look team take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow night.

Appointed as the club's new manager during the international break, Frick's reign got off to a flyer as Aberdeen won 4-2 away at Kilmarnock on Saturday.

Renowned for a high-octane attacking style of play at his previous clubs, the 52-year-old Liechtensteiner has already generated a wave of positivity at Pittodrie.

Aberdeen will face a tough task against an in-form Rangers side who are unbeaten in their last 13 matches.

But Frick insists there is no prospect of his team turning up at Ibrox and parking the bus in their efforts to take a positive result.

'I'm looking forward to it and I'm pretty confident in our squad,' he said. 'Now we have to prove that and have another good performance.

'That's not our style (to sit in and defend). We want to play like we did at Kilmarnock. That's our style of play.

Frick is all smiles after his side put four goals past Kilmarnock in his first match in charge

'Rangers will be a tough game. They are very strong, especially at home. I saw a lot of quality, particularly in their forward areas.

'We have to defend better than we did on Saturday, that's for sure, and that's what we're working on.

'I have to get to know my players even better because it's only been a week since we arrived in Aberdeen, and that takes time.

'But, of course, it helps when you win the first game. We've got some confidence now and I'm pretty confident we can take something from Ibrox.

'At the weekend, you could see that the mentality is very good. We struggled during the first 20 minutes of the second half, but the substitutes were very good and had a huge impact.

'I think, in the end, it was a deserved win and now we're looking forward to meeting Rangers at Ibrox.

'Defensively, we have to improve. Otherwise, it will be very difficult. I'm pretty sure we can defend better.

'But, like I say, we want to play like we did at the weekend. It's not our style (just to sit back and defend).'

Kevin Nisbet is mobbed by team-mates after netting the first of his double at Rugby Park

After the doom and gloom of the Stephen Robinson era, Frick has immediately created a feelgood factor at Aberdeen.

The fans were singing his name after the victory at Rugby Park on Saturday - and he wants to strengthen that feeling of unity throughout the club.

'It's been very good so far, especially with the win,' he added. 'The team has some confidence now and I see many players laughing.

'That's very important because we do this for fun as well. When you go onto the pitch, you have to take things seriously, but always with enjoyment. That's very important.

'The relationship between the team and the supporters is important, not between the supporters and me, because the team is the most important thing.

'For the players' confidence, it was very important that so many supporters travelled to Kilmarnock and celebrated the win with us. That was the first step.

'It's not the time for me to make a statement. It's the first time we're playing together at Ibrox, and it's important that we stick to our style of play.

'That's the most important thing to me. It is an exciting game and we are looking forward to it.'

#1821. Man United predicted lineup vs. Brentford: Cunha, Shaw, Dalot decisions for Pochettino

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 16:05, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 18:42

Manchester United will be without at least three players for Saturday’s Premier League clash with Brentford at Old Trafford.

Carlos Baleba (hamstring), Benjamin Sesko (calf) and Manuel Ugarte (knee) all remain sidelined with injuries, while Marcus Rashford (hip), Luke Shaw (fitness), Karl Darlow (knee) and captain Bruno Fernandes (illness) will all be assessed ahead of kickoff, the latter of whom missed training on Friday.

Shaw watched on as an unused substitute on Wednesday as Man United drew 2-2 with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, and the left-back may be ready to start his first game since October 10.

If not, then Lisandro Martinez could be tasked with a start on the left side of a back four where he began against Sporting, while Diogo Dalot will hope to force his way back into the first XI at right-back ahead of Noussair Mazraoui.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card overturned following his eighth-minute dismissal in United’s 4-0 Premier League defeat at Liverpool last weekend. The Frenchman is likely to start alongside Harry Maguire at centre-back, with Matthijs de Ligt to continue as a substitute.

Youri Tielemans was sent off for two bookable offences against Sporting, but he is available to start in midfield on Saturday alongside Kobbie Mainoo, while Fernandes - if fit - will continue in the number 10 role seeking to build on his brace netted in midweek.

Matheus Cunha served a continental ban against Sporting and is now free to return to Mauricio Pochettino’s side against Brentford, with either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee set to drop out as a result.

If Amad reverts to the bench, former Brentford attacker Bryan Mbeumo could move over to the right flank, but if Zirkzee makes way, Mbeumo will presumably lead the line as Cunha operates on the left flank.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha; Zirkzee

#1820. Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

🗣️ "We started to tire in the second half"Millwall manager Alex Neil shares his thoughts on this afternoon's Dockers Derby, after the Lions drew 2-2 with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/xnmubZ9NIz

🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o

Asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil said: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”

"It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever played in..I got shivers walking out"Millwall's Caleb Taylor speaks to Aaron Paul following today's 2-2 draw with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/yFoRuxooe6

Will there be one final chance? Sturge earns a throw-in on the far side and Dykes limbers up... But West Ham clear their lines and that is that. It ends two goals apiece.

Lisbie has looked dangerous down that left side and he just runs out of room under pressure from Mavropanos. The pair square up, with Lisbie sticking his finger into the Greek’s cheek.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

DYKES! 😱So close to a late winner for Millwall, but his shot flies over the bar. pic.twitter.com/fQFpQBdS7j

Neghli steps up to take it but it strikes the wall.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

Woah.. Kante gets his pocket picked by Lisbie on the half-way line and the West Ham goalscorer has no choice but to foul him as the last man. West Ham have a free-kick just outside the box.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

Pablo’s at it again, steaming his way into the left half-space, but Mazou-Sacko does well to track back and block the Brazilian’s effort. The resulting corner is gathered by Marschall who attempts to send Servais away but Kilman is wise to it and takes a booking for a professional foul.

Mazou-Sacko has his hands all over Pablo’s back and while the Brazilian is awarded a free-kick he slams the ball to the ground feeling he had broken free. He earns a booking for his troubles and the resulting free-kick comes to nothing.

Millwall 2 West Ham 2 (Mavropanos) Millwall are finally undone by a cross. Bowen goes short with a corner and Solomon dinks the ball on to the Greek defender’s head and he plants the ball past Marschall. The away end erupts...

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

It’s Bowen’s turn to try an effort at goal. Metcalfe does brilliantly to charge it down but there is no respite for Millwall as Kante’s long-range sighter goes behind for another corner.

That goal has changed the dynamic of this match. Millwall have dropped into a back five and West Ham are all over them. Bowen earns his side a corner and his delivery comes out to Solomon on the edge of the box, and while Cooper is able to partially clear, Austbo stings the gloves of Marschall from distance to win another corner.

Millwall 2 West Ham 1 (Kante) The substitute strokes a right-footed effort into the bottom corner from outside the box. A great finish.

GOAL for West Ham!Kante finds the back of the net with a clinical finish from outside the box.Can the Hammers draw level? pic.twitter.com/0RZO8oqrtR

Bowen hangs up a corner but Millwall clear their lines with ease. The hosts look so comfortable defending balls into the box.

The versatile defender Baggott is on for Sykes. ITV have just shown a replay of the “spitting” incident but it’s really difficult to make anything out from that distance.

The resulting corner comes to nothing. ITV are relaying reports of a counter-claim from Millwall that Castellanos might have spat in Marschall’s direction.

Chance! Bowen stands up a delightful cross and Pablo forces Marschall into a fine stop. Corner awarded.

Some confusion here as Marschall appears to have taken too long over a goal-kick, and while most believe that a West Ham corner had been awarded, it ends up being a goal-kick.

The ITV commentators say that West Ham are alleging that Marschall spat in Pablo’s direction.

Arconte chases down a lost cause and telescopes a leg through Taylor to earn a corner. He spins around to the home supporters and windmills his arms in their direction as the volume increases. Metcalfe’s cross is well overhit, though, and sails out for a goal-kick.

Kante’s runs in behind are threatening to disrupt Millwall’s backline shape, but Neil’s midfield sentries Mazou-Sacko and Metcalfe are doing such a great job to cover the gaps that the hosts still look like they have things under control.

A thunderous chant of “Milllllllll” echoes around the ground as the home fans spur their charges on.

Oof. Metcalfe leaves a foot in on Morato, his studs going into the defender’s Achilles. He should perhaps consider himself lucky to avoid punishment there. One that VAR may have intervened on in the Premier League.

Penalty shout! Metcalfe drives forward into the right of the box and Kante, who is hot pursuit, pushes the midfielder to the ground. Tierney immediately waves away the appeals and replays concur that the contact is probably not strong enough to warrant a penalty.

Bowen is presented with some grass to run into but his cross is well cleared. He gets another bite at the cherry, trying his luck from the edge of the box and Marschall just about gets to the rebound ahead of an onrushing Kante. A corner is awarded which the Millwall stopper flaps at but his team-mates are able to avert the danger.

West Ham earn a chance to deliver a corner from the near side but Engel’s inswinger finds Marschall’s gloves. Really poor.

Millwall continue leveraging Cooper and Taylor’s height in the box off set-pieces. Here, Metcalfe’s free-kick skims off the top of Cooper’s head but just misses the mark.

It looks like West Ham have gone to three at the back as Kante joins Mukasa and Engels in midfield. He’ll look to make late runs in behind.

Entering the West Ham box, he attempts to hold off Cooper but Osei-Tutu snaps in and earns a free-kick.

Two changes from Nuno, who takes off Piroe and Walker-Peters for Pablo and Kante.

Millwall have been good value for their lead, taking 16 shots and creating three big chances. West Ham, conversely have managed just one shot, off-target, despite controlling two-thirds of possession.

Arne Engel’s heatmap suggests he’s spent most of the match inside or just in advance of West Ham’s defensive third, which is not where Nuno will want either him or Divine Mukasa. The West Ham head coach could be tempted into changes at the break.

This is no more than Millwall – and West Ham – deserve. Sykes’s outrageous 35-yard strike deserved a goal and Neghli makes sure justice is served on the stroke of half-time. The roar that greets the players leaving the field is deafening.

The Den is in dreamland. Millwall take a two-goal advantage into the break and Neil celebrates with unbridled delight on the touchline. A caveat, though... Millwall did spurn a 2-0 lead in their most recent match away at Middlesbrough.

Millwall 2 West Ham 0 (Neghli) It’s come from yet another Dykes long throw, which West Ham have failed to clear. The ball falls to the feet of Neghli in the six-yard box and he spears the ball beyond Hermansen and Bowen on the line. And that’s the half.

"It's DREAMLAND at the Den!!"🫶🏼Millwall snatch a second goal before the break, as Neghli drills it home.An unbelievable half from the home side. pic.twitter.com/NIfSmwkHXh

Chance! Sykes from 30 yards strikes the ball cleanly and his ferocious effort beats Hermansen all ends up but ricochets off the woodwork and away to safety. Two minutes of time added on, by the way...

WHAT A HIT!! 💥Sykes' long-range effort RATTLES the crossbar. A potential contender for goal of the season, had that gone into the net... pic.twitter.com/ivBOslIZaO

Millwall, for the umpteenth time, find themselves in a two-vs-two situation on the beak, as Arconte tries to twist Kilman one way and then the other. He sets the ball to Metcalfe but the contact is not great and Hermansen gathers.

West Ham threaten Millwall’s lead momentarily as Mukasa breaks down their right, but Marschall does well to smother the ball and earns a free-kick on the process.

There’s a muted appeal for a penalty as Mavropanos nudges Cooper to the floor, but it’s a soft contact which takes place outside of the box anyhow.

Castellanos then attempts to burst down the right but Mazou-Sacko, who has been fantastic thus far, steams in and boots the ball out of play before geeing up the crowd.

Another foul... Osei-Tutu jumps into Morato but West Ham give the free-kick straight back to their opponents.

Morato leaves a leg in as Osei-Tutu attempts to break free, perhaps in retaliation to the earlier discretion, and he earns the first booking of the match.

It’s seven-seven in the fouls contest for those wondering, the latest being a mistimed challenge on Sykes by Castellanos near the right touchline. Millwall pump another ball into the box which is not up to much.

In an attempt to get his foot on the ball, Engels has often peeled out to the right-back position, but a wild, desperate cross-field ball that goes straight to Osei-Tutu sums up West Ham’s half aptly.

A wild challenge from Metcalfe on Cooper earns West Ham a free-kick and its then Sykes’ turn to land a late tackle, this time in the right channel. The subsequent delivery finds Castellanos but he cannot direct the ball goalwards.

West Ham’s strength comes from the fluidity of their front four, but Nuno’s creators have not been able to access them. So effective has Millwall’s back-line coverage been that West Ham have only managed low-quality final-third entries.

For the first time this half, Millwall begin to retreat deep into their own half, their lines of defence merging. And while West Ham tot up a fair number of passes on the edge of the box, they ultimately cede possession and Millwall spring a counter. Arconte appears to be through but Kilman does well to recover and Dykes’ subsequent shot is charged down.

West Ham are not learning their lessons and Sturge almost pulls off a similar pass in behind for Arconte, but the linesman raises his flag on this occasion. Replays show that it was really tight.

Millwall are going man-to-man as West Ham try to build and the visitors are struggling to get out. Sturge works infield from his starting perch on the left and almost threads a through-ball in behind for Arconte to gallop on to but Kilman does well to stick in a boot.

West Ham are desperately trying to calm this game down, but the Millwall fans are making that quite the challenge. The visitors string a series of passes together before Bowen strays offside.

Millwall then burst forward, Arconte this time popping up in a dangerous position on the right but Metcalfe fires over having picked off a loose Hammers pass out from the back.

Another Dykes throw-in sparks panic in West Ham’s box. Osei-Tutu’s back-post header appears to take a deflection off Walker-Peters, but the referee awards a goal-kick.

Millwall 1 West Ham 0 (Taylor) If at first you don’t succeed, try and try again... Dykes’ long throw from the right prompts chaos on the West Ham box and although Hermansen is able to keep out efforts from Sykes and Arconte, he can’t deny Taylor from close range. Cue bedlam in the stands. A massive, massive goal.

Or not… The Den erupts! That was appalling defending from a long throw and West Ham got exactly what they deserved, with Mads Hemansen’s brilliant save failing to spare them.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

It is all Millwall so far. They have been first to pretty much every ball and are giving West Ham no time on it at all. Konstantinos Mavropanos has just bought the visitors a breather after going down injured.

Hermansen gets caught in no-man’s land as Millwall spin in another ball from deep. It falls to the feet of Dykes but his effort does not have the requisite power to beat Kilman on the line.

Mavropanos appears to have been taken out by his own goalkeeper in the commotion and receives some on-field medical treatment.

Neil will be happy with how his side have started this match. Their intensity off the ball has forced West Ham into errors and here Sturge picks Bowen’s pocket on the halfway line before picking out Arconte in the box. He tries to squeeze a shot through Mukasa but the young midfielder does well to clear his lines.

The resulting corner comes out to Mazou-Sacko on the edge of the box but his effort sails over the bar.

Dykes and Arconte are Millwall’s attacking threats and the former wins a free-kick in the left channel. The hosts load the box with their biggest aerial threats but Metcalfe’s teasing inswinger just evades everyone. Tierney blows up for a foul anyhow...

There’s a minor clash off the ball as Morato and Cooper exchange words. Paul Tierney speaks with both players before Dykes launches a long throw into the box which is cleared and Hermansen is wise to the subsequent cross off the second phase.

Arconte tiptoes into the West Ham box and picks out Sturge whose miscued shot finds Metcalfe on the edge of the box. His effort is straight at Hermansen who collects the ball calmly.

That Jenson Metcalfe tackle on West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen came after just 15 seconds. What Vinny Jones might call “a reducer”.

"That's the expectation, I would imagine" 😅The first free-kick is awarded just 12 seconds into Millwall's derby against West Ham.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/qpxjQEKN6x

Millwall launch a free-kick from deep into the box after Castellanos gives away a needless foul and after some pinball Hermansen gathers.

It took just 13 seconds for us to get our first foul. Kudos to anyone who had that in their Dockers Derby sweepstake... A late lunge from Metcalfe on Bowen.

And the players emerge, Hey Jude now being played... Millwall are in their customary navy-blue home strip and white shorts. West Ham are giving their new white away kit a first outing.

There’s just about enough time for the two sides to meet for quick summits before Millwall get us under way!

The atmosphere is building nicely in the ground and the players are now lined up in the tunnel, Cooper and Bowen standing shoulder to shoulder.

Seats are filling up rapidly with barely 10 minutes before kick-off, with the away end a notable exception. The home fans are making their own presence felt as The Jam’s A Town Called Malice and The Clash’s London Calling blare out over the public-address system.

"The fans are up for it, the players are up for it" 💪🏼Lyndon Dykes looks ahead to today's match, and reflects on his strong start to life as a Millwall player.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/V9nPzbh3Ob

Kevin Nolan, West Ham’s captain, was sent off early but his team-mates defied the odds to win 2-1 thanks to goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid either side of a stunning Liam Trotter strike.

In Millwall’s match-day squad that day were… Harry Kane and Ryan Mason.

The last time West Ham and Millwall met, Harry Kane was a Millwall player 😅This is how that game in 2012 played out 👇 pic.twitter.com/OhtVx3caCP

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

“There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” says a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd

There have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means…

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

On potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY

Riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

Alex Neil names his Lions XI 👊 pic.twitter.com/MP0N9wMatG

Just the one change from the league leaders’ last league match as Kyle Walker-Peters comes in for the injured Joel Veltman.

Today's teamsheet 📋 pic.twitter.com/EmrxYRhsPd

"We have to quiet them down" 🤫West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen is expecting a hostile atmosphere at The Den today 🗣️Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/9tp2225Rq8

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

#1819. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Also, it was Pulisics’ pass to Moreira that set-up Cisse’s goal. If were recognizing “hockey assists” then Pulisic’s pass to Moreira was also world-class. Not to be a wet-blanket, but Moreira and Cisse need to develop composure on the ball. Too often Moreira would negate his speed on the ball by dribbling into multiple defenders without looking to pass to an open teammate. Against the top teams Milan will not have as many goal scoring opportunities as they did on Sunday so now is the time to work on finding the open man in the final third.

So young players with potential, need to learn to be better and realise thier potential.

It was a pass in a 3v3 counter-attack situation. Great pass but Modric took out 5 defenders with 1 move. That is why it is world class and Pulisic pass is not mentioned as much.

Did anyone notice how Pulisic slowed down his run, thus letting Ramos reach the penalty box earlier and score his long awaited goal? Such a team player..

He’s always been that guy. Sometimes I wish he can be more ‘selfish’. Another example is the penalty fiasco with Tammy back then.

Yet some people here have called him selfish many times – especially last season when he wasn’t scoring. But then again, those same people praised Leao and probably thought he was Ballon d’Or material. LOL. 🤦‍♂️😂😂😂

Yes. I’d say it was as much about letting Ramos score as it was about “arriving” in the box late, setting up a cut back score, which he learned from Frank Lampard. Both are good things.

#1818. Joshua Kimmich blasts Bayern Munich board over Jamal Musiala health situation

Joshua Kimmich has hit out at Bayern Munich’s hierarchy over their comments about Jamal Musiala’s health situation.

Musiala collapsed in two different games in the space of four days during Bayern’s pre-season campaign in the summer and revealed that he had been suffering from ‘absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction’.

The 23-year-old’s start to the season was also disrupted due to a thigh injury and the midfielder has started just one game in the Bundesliga so far.

Last week, Bayern’s supervisory board member, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, suggested that Musiala may be offered a pay cut due to his health situation and claims no club would buy the midfielder ‘under these conditions’.

Earlier this month, Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, also raised questions about Musiala’s contract due to his health issue.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Speaking after Bayern’s 2-1 defeat away to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Kimmich described the club’s actions towards Musiala as ‘completely incomprehensible’.

‘Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I completely understand that this isn’t an easy situation for a club either,’ Kimmich said.

‘Of course, I’ve followed Jamal’s journey over the last two years. I mean, he carried us at the European Championship and was our standout player afterwards. Then he extended his contract, got the number 10 shirt here and for the German national team. Then came the first muscle injury. I can say from my own experience, when you extend your contract, especially at that age, it’s not about sitting back and enjoying the next five years. It’s an incentive and a challenge you want to live up to.

‘Then Jamal had the illness and the serious injury. We mustn’t forget that in the last year and a half, I don’t think he’s played four or five games in a row.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So, to a certain extent, it’s understandable that he’s not at that level. And it’s also understandable that the club is worried because of the illness. What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It should never happen that this is played out at the expense of a player.

‘Of course, the club is always the highest priority and is bigger than us as players but still not bigger than the individual. And that is an absolute no-go and not in the spirit of Bayern, especially in the current phase, where I myself have often emphasised how very, very special the club is.

‘Even in my own situation, the club was very, very special. You could really feel that this ‘Mia san mia’ spirit was truly lived. What has happened now should simply never happen. I find it completely incomprehensible.’

Asked if he has spoken with Musiala about the comments from Bayern’s hierarchy, Kimmich said: ‘Honestly, I get the impression that Jamal isn’t aware of everything that’s going on out there. I think that’s actually a good thing.

‘Of course, there was some discussion. For me, the most important thing is that he comes to Sabener Strasse every day and enjoys playing football. That’s the most important thing in his situation.

‘You also mustn’t forget that he had another operation in the summer and then suffered another injury. But I see him and experience him every day. I see how he works, how hard he works. That also adds to the situation. It’s not that he has problems because he’s unprofessional, rather, he’s there every day, naturally wants to get the most out of himself, works very, very hard every day, and I think he enjoys being with us in the team. I hope he feels that we all stand behind him 100 per cent – ​​the team, the management, and the club.’

#1817. Celtic accept ticket reduction for Tynecastle despite fury of fans

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 23 November 2026

Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.

The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the issue.

Celtic will receive 508 tickets for the Premiership encounter on November 29, which will be their first visit to Tynecastle since beating Hearts to the title in the final stages of last season, a victory which resulted in a pitch invasion from some of their fans at Celtic Park.

A Celtic statement read: 'As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20 per cent, compared to our previous visit.

'There have been a variety of views expressed to the club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation.

'We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland.

Hearts had stated that only 508 tickets will be made available for Celtic fans on November 29

'Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets.

'We respect all views and opinions on this matter, and while we are concerned and disappointed at this reduction, and others across recent years, we feel it is important that the team has the backing of our fans within the stadium for an important match.

'We realise the difficulties such a reduction can cause and in light of our discussions with supporters, we can confirm that should any supporter who is successful in the ballot, but does not wish to accept this ticket, then this will NOT affect the away ticket record moving forward.

'We thank our fans for their continued support and can confirm that we will be discussing the matter further with both the home club and the SPFL.'

Celtic and Rangers formerly received the full Roseburn Stand for their supporters at Tynecastle, which resulted in an allocation of almost 3,500 tickets.

However, that figure was reduced to about 1,250 tickets in the 2021-22 season amid increased demand from home fans after the lockdown, and was further cut by about half.

Only Hibernian now get the full Roseburn Stand in a reciprocal agreement between the Edinburgh rivals.

Tynecastle has a capacity of about 20,000 but Hearts’ attendances are normally around 18,700 as a number of seats are not in use to create a barrier between the home and away fans.

Visiting clubs get about 800 tickets for games at Celtic Park, which has a 60,000 capacity.

#1816. Could Pep Guardiola succeed Thomas Tuchel as England manager after revealing his 'next step'?

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 16:12

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has confirmed that he wants to move into international management when he returns to football, an admission that raises an intriguing question about England's long-term plans beyond Thomas Tuchel's tenure.

The Spaniard has been taking a break from management since leaving the Etihad Stadium at the end of the 2025-26 season, bringing an end to a remarkable decade in which he won six Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Although Guardiola has yet to establish a date for his return, the 55-year-old has a clear idea of what he wants to do next. His latest comments also shed light on how close he came to embarking on an international career last summer, when the Italian Football Federation approached him about taking charge of the Azzurri.

Speaking in an interview with his former Barcelona teammate Romario on Romario TV, Guardiola was asked whether there was a team he had never managed but would like to coach.

"A national team, which is my next step," replied the former Bayern Munich boss, who also explained that the timing of Italy's approach had prevented him from accepting the position.

"If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted," Guardiola admitted, explaining that his conversations with Paolo Maldini and Leonardo had taken place when he felt he needed a break from football.

Having spent 18 years in club management, Guardiola was reluctant to commit himself to another project so soon after leaving City. Italy subsequently appointed Roberto Mancini, while the Spaniard remains without a managerial position and has given no indication of when his sabbatical will end.

The United States are another potential destination following Mauricio Pochettino's departure to Manchester United. Guardiola has previously spoken enthusiastically about the potential of the American national team, although the prospect of managing England may also warrant consideration given the Football Association's reported interest in him in the past.

According to The Athletic, Guardiola was the FA's preferred candidate to replace Gareth Southgate following Euro 2024, with a verbal agreement reportedly in place before the Spaniard opted to remain at Manchester City.

His former Spain teammate Gaizka Mendieta has also identified England as a potential destination, alongside Brazil, believing that Guardiola would be attracted by the opportunity to compete for major international honours.

England's current managerial situation could prove compatible with Guardiola's desire to take an extended break. Tuchel signed a contract extension in February to lead the Three Lions through to Euro 2028 and reiterated his commitment to that agreement earlier this month.

The German, however, has also made no secret of his desire to return to club management once his England tenure comes to an end. Should he depart after the European Championship, his successor would have two years to prepare the national team for the 2030 World Cup.

By that stage, Guardiola would have spent two seasons away from the dugout. The prospect of working with players such as Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Phil Foden would certainly be interesting from a tactical perspective, particularly given his preference for technically accomplished midfielders capable of operating in several positions.

His familiarity with English football and previous experience of working with several England internationals would also ease certain aspects of the transition, although implementing his demanding tactical approach within the limited training windows available to national team managers would represent a new challenge.

There is currently nothing to suggest that the FA are looking beyond Tuchel or that Guardiola has identified England as his preferred destination. However, should the position become available in 2028, the circumstances could be considerably more favourable than when the FA reportedly approached him two years ago.

#1813. David Raya injury update as expert explains if Arsenal star can play against Man City

Arsenal hope David Raya has avoided a serious shoulder injury but their goalkeeper is still likely to be a doubt for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.

The Spain international injured his shoulder in a rather innocuous incident during last weekend’s draw with Newcastle United, making contact with William Osula while claiming a cross.

Raya was left in considerable pain with Sky Sports forced to apologise for initially playing down the incident. The former Brentford star trudged off the pitch clutching his arm to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, who started in his place in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Raya was visibly distressed on Saturday night and it prompted huge concerns over the man who has been so pivotal to Arsenal’s rise to the summit of English football. While boasting the most formidable squad in the Premier League, Raya is simply irreplaceable.

The outlook was brighter this week with Mikel Arteta revealing his goalkeeper will not require surgery.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment,’ Arteta told the media earlier this week.

‘The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.’

Arsenal have not disclosed any specific details over the injury but it seems clear at this stage Raya is not facing the sort of layoff that kept Nick Pope out for over four months after he suffered a dislocated shoulder in 2023.

They will hope any layoff is a short-term one heading into the festive period with a trip to the Etihad now looming large this weekend. Kepa was trusted with a starting role against City in the Carabao Cup final ahead of Raya back in March, having started in every previous round of the competition, but was at fault at Wembley that day as Pep Guardiola’s side claimed the first silverware of the season.

There was plenty of panic on Saturday night as Raya made his way off the pitch at St James’ Park. While Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes are pivotal figures, there is simply no replacing their no1.

Pundits lined up fearing the worst for Arsenal at the weekend with Jamie Redknapp suggesting any absence will ‘change everything for Arsenal for a while.’

Read more on what he and Arsenal legend Ian Wright said on the night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

While Arteta trusts Kepa, getting Raya back as soon as possible will be vital. Arsenal have sent reassuring messages this week but having him back in time for this weekend is likely to be a big ask.

‘It is so hard to tell how long he may be out for, we would want to know the full diagnosis,’ Stephen Smith, CEO and founder of Kitman Labs which specialises in injury welfare and performance analytics, told Metro.

‘All we have to use is the replay of the incident and how he looked coming off the pitch and he did look in incredible pain. He looked like someone who had dislocated his shoulder playing rugby. My guess is that if there was that much pain and discomfort immediately, this weekend would be too soon. That said, looking back at how innocuous it was, you would hope the length of his absence  would be the small number of weeks range.’

Arsenal have a relatively clean bill of health elsewhere in the squad with Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka their only other absences.

Saka’s latest injury is likely to keep him out until Christmas with spells on the sidelines becoming increasingly regular for the winger.

Are a growing number of knocks coupled with the years of unrelenting game time taking their toll on the England international?

Read our deep dive into Saka’s injury history as the experts tell us if Arsenal have something to really be concerned with.

Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the league and don’t play a game outside of London until mid-January. But their run of fixtures in December could provide the most thorough examination of their ability to defend their crown this season.

The month starts with a trip to Raya’s old club Brentford, followed by the north London derby against a rejuvenated Tottenham. Real Madrid then come to town in the Champions League before Arsenal host Bournemouth, who walked away with the win on their last visit to north London. They then host Manchester United in their last game before Christmas.

Arteta will be expected to shed more light on Raya’s recovery period when he speaks to the press on Friday with he and his staff now likely to have a clear picture of what the injury is after further scans this week.

Raya is perhaps the most athletic goalkeeper in the league and ensuring he is able to reach his spectacular physical levels will be key in the coming days and weeks.

Smith explained the process will involve four stages to ensure Raya is pain-free before he returns to action.

‘Finding out surgery is not needed so quickly was very encouraging. My guess is after the second scan this week they will know exactly what it is at this point,’ he said.

‘In terms of recovery time, it all depends on exactly what it is. If it was a slight subluxation then they will be looking at letting that rest, recover and become pain free, allowing it to get a range of motion back before doing a small amount of strengthening work and get him back out there.

‘If it something closer to a rotator cuff strain it may take a little longer. Typically what they are looking at in this situation comes in four stages. The first is settling the pain and protecting the joint, the second is getting full range back, the third is rebuilding strength around it and fourth, which can take a bit more time, is position-specific loading.

‘When you think about the shoulder and what a goalkeeper is required to do – all their diving and landing, catching overhead, distributing the ball – it’s pretty demanding on the shoulder. So even if it is on the lower end of the scale from a structural damage perspective, it is still likely to require time to make sure he is capable of doing all that.

‘The first 48 hours will have been the most painful. But throughout the rehab process, they won’t want him to be sore. If he’s sore, that means potentially they aren’t giving it enough time. So they will want him to feel really comfortable and really strong.’

#1809. Motherwell vs Hibernian - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 26 Nov 2026 16:24

Motherwell and Hibernian will come together on Saturday evening for a Scottish Premiership clash at Fir Park.

The hosts are 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 13 points, while the visitors are ninth with 14 points.

Motherwell initially recorded a positive start to the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season, winning two and drawing two of their first four league games under new boss Alfred Johansson.

However, the Steelmen have subsequently recorded just one win in the following 10 league fixtures, alongside two draws and seven defeats.

That run included a particularly miserable six-game losing streak from September 5 to October 25, which was eventually ended by two draws and a win at the end of October and early November.

However, another defeat last weekend, a 2-1 loss to Rangers, has culminated in Motherwell falling to 11th in the standings with just 13 points from 14 games, leaving Johansson under increasing pressure.

Motherwell's biggest issue this term has been their lack of goals, with just 16 scored in 14 league games, although they have managed to find the back of the net in each of their last four matches.

Desperate to avoid slipping further away from safety and closer to the bottom, especially with 12th-placed Kilmarnock taking on 10th-placed St Mirren, Motherwell will be eager to pick up just their fourth league win of the season on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Hibernian head into Saturday's matchday 15 encounter in resurgent form, having won three, drawn one and lost just one of their last five games across all competitions.

The first of those triumphs saw Hibernian come from behind to defeat rivals Hearts 2-1 in the Scottish League Cup semi-final, securing their place in the final and marking Marink Reedijk's first win as manager.

The subsequent two victories, 4-0 against Aberdeen and 2-1 against Dundee, have both come in the league, helping Hibernian climb out of the relegation zone and into ninth place.

Hibernian will be looking to build on that improved form with another victory on Saturday, especially as they aim to continue climbing up the table - currently trailing sixth-placed St Johnstone by just three points.

#1808. Lee Dixon makes Man City Premier League title claim ahead of Arsenal clash

Lee Dixon thinks Manchester City’s Premier League title chances are far from over even if they fall to defeat against Arsenal on Sunday.

City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.

Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.

Bubbling away in the background remains the possibility of a huge points deduction after the club were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges for financial breaches.

And Dixon believes that such uncertainty might be playing on the minds of City’s players, telling Metro: ‘Nobody liked Arsenal under George Graham and we built up resilience because of that.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘I think that could have been happening for City at the start of the season with the charges, but that bounce can die off a bit and then all of a sudden, you’ve had a couple of bad results and it gets into your head.’

Arsenal could extend their lead over City to nine points with victory at the Emirates on Sunday, but Dixon believes that it would still be far too early to rule City out of this season’s title race.

‘As a fan, after seeing Arsenal get over the line last season, you now have something to fall back on and I do believe that, from a fan’s perspective, if you see Arsenal beat City on Sunday, you can think that’s it,’ he added.

‘However, as a player, you won’t see any of them coming out and going, “It’s done and dusted”, because City have so much quality. We all know that City could go on a ten-game winning streak, so they’ll always have that opportunity.
