#1748. Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

On TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their new head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

United’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M

But, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so important for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

In the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

It was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

It was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

The defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm

Fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. It is just one win in five for United, and it was another performance which was far from convincing. It could have been worse though, they were a few minutes away from losing. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

United break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

United may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M

Bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

United with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

You would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

Here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

Positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

Fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

Fulham have stopped playing since they scored, and they needed Leno again to tip a Cunha shot around the post. The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

What a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”

Well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN

Fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

Fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

Gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the new season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

More from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”

There has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

Sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

At half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

United’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

The game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

Mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

This stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

Fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

Fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

Bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

United have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

If Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

Michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

JJ Gabriel has been in the news this week, and Sam Wallace writes in his column this week that the battle to sign up and coming academy players is growing ever more fierce between Premier League clubs. Managers are handing out debuts earlier and earlier to satisfy the demands of the best young players, and an increasing number of clubs are happy to gamble significant fees and wages on potental.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia

Subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe

Here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊

The script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager said.

“That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1747. Di Marzio: Sporting CP striker emerges as idea for Milan amid Amorim’s admiration

AC Milan want to sign a striker in the winter transfer window, and Gianluca Di Marzio has put forward a new target.

Di Marzio has published an update on his website regarding Serie A clubs and the search for a centre-forward that many of them have commenced. He confirms that Milan are among the teams seeking attacking reinforcements, salso o they can loan Francesco Camarda out.

A name that’s been floating around for a few days – in addition to Endrick of Real Madrid and Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge – is Sporting CP’s Fotis Ioannidis. He’s a player that Ruben Amorim really likes, having kept a close eye on things in Portugal, but Roma are keen too.

Ioannidis is a name worth considering even if he may not be top of the list, given Milan are the ‘only team without spending constraints’ in Serie A. Cardinale has already shown that if he wants a player and Milan truly needs him, he’s ready to invest.

The 26-year-old has racked up two goals and two assists in 10 league games for the Lisbon-based club, who just welcomed Paulo Fonseca as their new head coach. Overall he has eight goals and six assists in 37 games (all competitions), plus seven in 26 for the Greece national team.

#1746. Arsenal XI vs Man City: David Raya injury latest, predicted lineup, confirmed team news for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal are set to make a late decision on the fitness of David Raya for Manchester City’s trip to north London on Sunday.

The goalkeeper missed Tuesday’s Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund due to a shoulder injury he picked up against Newcastle last weekend.

However, while there were fears that was a significant problem, scans have since showed that Raya avoided serious injury and his spell on the sidelines was not expected to be a lengthy one.

It remains to be seen whether Raya recovers in time to face City in the Premier League on Sunday, with Kepa Arrizabalaga ready to fill in again if required.

“I don’t know,” Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said of Raya’s availability at his pre-match press conference on Friday. “We still have a few hours before the game. We’re just trying to get everybody back.”

Asked whether there was hope that Raya would be available, Arteta added bluntly: “Yes.”

Ezri Konsa appears set to keep his place at centre-back alongside Gabriel, as Arsenal continue to cautiously manage William Saliba’s fitness.

Saliba was included in the matchday squad against both Newcastle and Dortmund but is yet to make a first-team appearance this season. It would be a surprise if he came straight in to face City.

It is expected that Riccardo Calafiori will return to the Arsenal starting lineup on Sunday after being rested in midweek, while Eberechi Eze could well get the nod in front of him on the left wing after impressing at St James’ Park.

Viktor Gyokeres scored against Dortmund but rival Kai Havertz is usually trusted in these biggest games by Arteta.

The German was given a full rest in that draw with Dortmund and he looks set to lead the line against City. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi both remain out with thigh and hamstring injuries respectively.

Predicted Arsenal XI vs Man City (4-2-3-1): Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz

#1745. Moreirense vs Santa Clara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:33

Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.

Moreirense spent much of the previous campaign in contention for a European place but eventually finished seventh, and they are currently some way off the pace in the race for a top-five finish following an inconsistent start to this season.

Vasco Botelho da Costa's men have won just four of their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L5), while struggling at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 18, the weakest defensive record among the current top-half sides.

The Moreira-based club enter this encounter on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon, which ended a two-match winning run following victories over Estoril Praia and Estrela Amadora.

Although losing by a single goal away to Sporting is hardly the most disappointing result, Da Costa will be concerned by a pattern that has seen his side suffer their last three defeats by the same 1-0 scoreline, including a Taca de Portugal exit at the hands of second-tier AVS.

Moreirense have also struggled for consistency on home soil this season, winning just two of their five league matches at Parque Moreira de Conegos (D1, L2), although a 2-1 victory over Estrela in their most recent outing at the venue gives them an opportunity to secure consecutive home wins for the first time since April and May.

Santa Clara, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to the Primeira Liga campaign, collecting 21 points from their opening 11 matches (W6, D3, L2), although Petit's side have recently seen the resilience that characterised their early-season performances begin to fade.

After going unbeaten in their first eight fixtures (W5, D3), the Azoreans have lost three of their last four competitive outings, beginning with a disappointing Taca de Portugal exit against lower-division Mafra before suffering a league defeat to Benfica.

Although they bounced back with a victory away to Maritimo, Santa Clara were beaten 2-1 by Gil Vicente in their most recent top-flight outing before playing out a 2-2 draw against Valladolid in a friendly on November 11.

Nevertheless, Petit's men remain among the hardest sides to break down in the division, having conceded just eight league goals, with only leaders Porto (five) boasting a better defensive record, while Santa Clara have scored twice as many at the other end.

Their away performances have been particularly impressive, with the Azoreans collecting 13 points from five league trips (W4, D1), giving them the third-best away record in this season's Primeira Liga behind Porto and Benfica.

However, the visitors have struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last four league meetings with Moreirense and losing three, including both encounters last season, which ended in 1-0 defeats.

Moreirense will welcome Tiago Andrade back into contention after the winger recovered from the muscle problem that ruled him out of the trip to Sporting.

Meanwhile, Alexandre Parsemain (leg) and Joao Veloso (muscle) remain doubts, while Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso are still recovering from their respective muscle injuries and are expected to remain unavailable.

With Parsemain's availability uncertain, Leonardo Vonic could lead the line once again, although Yan Maranho is another option in that position.

Santa Clara have considerably greater selection problems, with first-choice centre-backs Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira both suspended following their disciplinary issues against Gil Vicente, with the former receiving a red card and the latter missing out through an accumulation of bookings.

Petit's defensive options are further limited by the potential absence of Guilherme Romao, who is sidelined with injury, though Pedro Ferreira could return this weekend if he is fully fit following a nose issue.

As a result, Ythallo could make his senior debut alongside Henrique Silva in central defence, although both have limited first-team experience, having featured predominantly at youth level and as a substitute, respectively.

Goncalo Paciencia returned from injury as a second-half substitute last time out and could lead the line here, potentially leaving Fernando to make way.

There is also good  news in goal,  with Lucas Franca having recovered from a muscle injury and expected to return to contention for the starting role.

A Ferreira; Pinto, Kevyn Monteiro, Batista, A Martinez; N John, Liberato; Andrade, Mendonca, Landerson; Vonic

Franca; Lucas Soares, Ythallo, H Silva, Fofana; Tavares, Borges, Vasconcelos; V Lopes, Paciencia, B Lucas

Santa Clara have been considerably stronger away from home this season, but their defensive absences could prove costly against a Moreirense side that have won three of the last four meetings between the clubs.

Furthermore, the hosts have an opportunity to exploit an inexperienced centre-back pairing, although their own scoring problems and the visitors' impressive away record suggest neither side will have enough to claim all three points.

#1744. The truth behind Manchester United triggering Bruno Fernandes contract extension

Manchester United had the January transfer window in mind when triggering Bruno Fernandes’ contract extension.

Standard Sport understands that Man Utd have activated their option to extend their captain’s deal by one year.

Fernandes’ current terms were due to expire at the end of the current season, but now run until the summer of 2028.

Fernandes confirmed last week that he had put contract negotiations with United on hold due to the club’s ongoing struggles on the pitch, having already rejected two offers of new terms.

Man Utd head into the Premier League weekend sitting in 19th place in the Premier League, and welcome sixth-placed Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday in what is new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge.

Fernandes has struggled to reproduce the form that earned him a host of individual awards last season, and Standard Sport understands that both parties believe it is sensible to return to negotiations at a later date.

Pochettino hints at Fernandes injury in shock blow to Man Utd plans

#1743. Manchester United XI vs Brentford: Bruno Fernandes latest, predicted lineup, confirmed team news for Premier League

Bruno Fernandes is a doubt for Manchester United as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to welcome Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday.

The club captain was unable to train on Friday morning due to a virus, which has thrown into doubt his involvement in Pochettino’s first home match in charge.

Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his new team, and this is a potentially huge spanner to throw into the works.

Fernandes’s absence could see Matheus Cunha move into the No10 role, supported by Amad Diallo and Patrick Dorgu, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Elsewhere, the new manager also has a decision to make in defence. Having opted for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Pochettino switched to a four-man defence for the chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday, in which Fernandes scored both goals.

Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, a more timid back three seems unlikely.

It will be a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.

Pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game.

Brentford’s pace in behind may necessitate a quicker backline, meaning Maguire could make way again here, having also reportedly complained of an injury after the midweek match.

Lisandro Martinez has been at left-back, but Dorgu’s attacking qualities will likely be required on Saturday and Luke Shaw is also now back in training. By moving Martinez back to centre-half alongside Yoro, Pochettino can find the pace required. Diogo Dalot may get the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Fernandes was deployed on the left behind Cunha in the defeat by Liverpool, while Mbeumo was briefly used as the lone forward under Michael Carrick.

Here, we’re predicting Cunha to lead the line after his midweek rest due to suspension, with Fernandes in behind as the No10 and Mbeumo on the left wing.

If Amad is fit enough to start after being forced off in the draw with Sporting, expect the Ivorian on the right flank. If not, youngster Shea Lacey could be a candidate to start.

#1742. Academico de Viseu vs Alverca - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:49

Coming off a three-week break from competitive action, Academico de Viseu and Alverca meet at Estadio do Fontelo on Saturday evening in what will be their first-ever encounter in Portugal's top flight.

The hosts occupy sixth place in the Primeira Liga table, eight points and five positions ahead of their visitors, who are four points above the relegation play-off spot.

Academico de Viseu have made an encouraging return to the top flight after a 37-year absence, having collected six wins from their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L3), scoring 15 times and conceding 13 at the other end.

Bruno Pinheiro's side, who failed to record a victory in any of their first four outings this term, enjoyed a particularly impressive spell between September 6 and November 1, winning six consecutive league matches, including a famous triumph away to Sporting Lisbon on October 25.

However, that winning run in the top flight came to an end last time out, when the Viseu club suffered a 1-0 defeat to Nacional in Funchal after conceding a late winner to Matchoi Djalo.

The result also means Academico have now alternated between defeats and victories across their last five matches in all competitions, including cup losses to lower-division Fatima in the Taca de Portugal and Primeira Liga champions Porto in the Taca da Liga.

Returning from a three-week hiatus, the Viseu club will be glad to be back at Fontelo, where they have won each of their last three matches, beating Vitoria de Guimaraes, Estoril Praia and Rio Ave by 2-1 scorelines after losing their opening two fixtures at the ground this term.

Like the hosts, Alverca also started the campaign slowly, failing to record a victory in any of their opening five fixtures, but enjoyed a three-match winning run between September 12 and October 12, beating Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao.

However, the Ribatejo club have slipped back into familiar struggles, having since gone winless in four matches across all competitions, starting with a Taca de Portugal elimination at the hands of second-tier Tondela before suffering narrow league defeats against Arouca and Benfica.

Sergio Ferreira's team then drew 1-1 with Casa Pia in their most recent outing, with Ian Luccas finding the net in the 66th minute to rescue a point, while the goal ended a three-match run without scoring.

Two wins from their last three league games on the road suggest Alverca have also held their own away from home, although they have been vulnerable when not at their best, losing three of their five away league outings this season.

There is also little to draw from history, given the Ribatejo club are without a victory in their previous three meetings with Academico, losing twice in that spell, although their most recent visit to Viseu ended in a 2-2 draw in February 2025 in Liga 2.

Academico de Viseu form (all competitions):

With no reported injury or suspension concerns, Academico head coach Pinheiro could retain a similar lineup to the one that featured against Nacional, with goalkeeper Ewerton shielded by the defensive quartet of Anthony Correia, Nikolaos Michelis, Robinho and Miguel Angel Brau.

Andre Clovis has scored five of the Viseu club's 15 league goals this season and also provided an assist, with the Brazilian expected to lead the line here.

Alverca could be without Rayan Lucas, who remains a doubt after suffering another setback with his left knee, although the midfielder has returned to integrated training.

Nabil Touaizi is also expected to miss out after suffering a relapse of a right-calf injury, while Bastien Meupiyou and Sabit Abdulai remain sidelined following knee surgery.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Noah Raveyre is another absentee, with his return expected in early December.

Academico de Viseu possible starting lineup:

Ewerton; Robinho, Correia, Michelis, Brau; L Silva, Messeguem; Guilherme, Kahraman, Mortimer; Clovis

Mendes; Boyan, Gomez, James; Spencer, I Luccas, Gui, Chissumba; Chiquinho, Camara, Figueiredo

Academico have struggled to find the net in recent weeks, but their overall league form and stronger position in the table make them worthy favourites against an Alverca side that have scored just once in their last four matches, so a home victory looks plausible.

#1741. Watch: Amorim’s passionate ‘biggest mistake’ response which achieved viral status

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he said.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your plan. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear plan, don’t look at the table.

“Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

“So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

“Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear plan what to do.”

🚨🎙️🔥 Ruben Amorim on Milan’s transfer strategy: “The BIGGEST mistake is looking at the table and saying: ‘We’re close, let’s spend CRAZY money.’”

“We have a CLEAR long-term plan and we won’t change it because of the table.”

“We want players with the right CHARACTER — not BIG STARS. Young is better right now.”

— Milan Wire (@MilanWireX) November 21, 2026

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

From a fans point of view, if one big signing is the difference between scudetto and not scudetto, I would tend to disagree with Amorim.

I think his point is that it’s about making the right signings. ACM has made panic buys the last couple of years. Stick to the plan. I think Arsenal is the perfect example of this approach.

Yeah, Joao Felix and Santi GImenez were big money, so was Nkunku. But if they don’t have the right characteristics and don’t fit the squad, then they will be a net negative to the team as a whole,

It’s not good enough to say, we are 1 or 2 players away from competing, we need to go buy some random hype player. You need to buy the RIGHT players that fit the team and the existing players.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that Dejan Kulusevski is closing in on his first Tottenham start in more than a year and a half.

Kulusevski made an emotional return to fitness last month, coming off the bench for his first appearance in 526 days following a serious patella injury as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The Swedish playmaker has since seen his minutes managed, with cameo appearances against Chelsea, Crystal Palace and Leeds before the international break.

Kulusevski was subsequently called up to Sweden’s squad for their Nations League fixtures against Bosnia and Poland earlier this month, playing a combined 54 minutes for Graham Potter’s side.

Spurs remain cautious about risking Kulusevski. But the 26-year-old’s performances over the international break have now convinced De Zerbi that he is nearly ready to start for the first time since Spurs’ 2-0 defeat to Crystal Palace on May 11, 2025.

#1739. Man United's January transfer budget will be less than £50m with Mauricio Pochettino expected to make only TWO signings - despite needing to bolster their attack and defence

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

It’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s new financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

United also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January

Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre)

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

#1738. Man City XI vs Arsenal: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester City head to Arsenal this weekend in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after only 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose again in north London on Sunday.

City are also still waiting for their appeal to be heard against the guilty verdict returned by an independent panel back in September on their charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18. They deny any wrongdoing.

Maresca has to find the right team to beat an Arsenal side that have lost just twice at home across all competitions in 2026.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will start in goal as usual, with the back four in front of him likely consisting of Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol.

Dias was rested for the home draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday night, with the City captain set to be restored to the starting XI here.

Nico O’Reilly has emerged as the first-choice option at left-back in recent weeks, but the defensive ability of Gvardiol could be key in a potentially cagey match.

Maresca has experimented with the construction of his midfield in the last few games. Enzo Fernandez was deployed as a No10 against Napoli, but a return to the preferred paring of the Argentine and Elliot Anderson at the base of City’s midfield feels likely at Arsenal.

Similarly, Iliman Ndiaye has impressed on the right wing in recent weeks. Rayan Cherki was deployed out wide against Napoli, but has been most effective as a No10.

Jeremy Doku has become trusted on the left, while Erling Haaland cannot be left out - even if he is enduring a goalscoring drought by his usual lofty standards.

Maresca revealed at his pre-match press conference on Friday that Antoine Semenyo was close to returning from a knee injury sustained against Ipswich last month, though the trip to Arsenal will come too soon for his comeback.

#1736. Real Madrid's £68m Nico Paz transfer plan faces fresh uncertainty as Jose Mourinho responds

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 20:55

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has declined to discuss the potential return of Nico Paz to the Santiago Bernabeu amid conflicting reports in Spain over the club's intention to activate their £68m buy-back option for the Como midfielder.

The Argentina international continues to impress in Italian football, registering six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as one of Europe's most exciting young attacking midfielders.

Madrid retained the option to bring Paz back in the summer of 2027 when an agreement was reached with Como in June to allow the 22-year-old to continue his development in Serie A. However, despite recent suggestions that the Spanish giants have already decided to exercise that option, uncertainty remains over their plans.

Asked about Paz during his press conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, Mourinho offered a typically brief response: "He's not my player."

The Portuguese manager's reluctance to discuss a player contracted to another club should not be interpreted as opposition to the transfer, although his response offered little clarification following contrasting reports in the Spanish media.

Cadena COPE reported last week that Real Madrid intended to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option next summer, with Como having reportedly been informed of the decision.

However, according to Jose Felix Diaz of AS, Madrid have yet to reach a definitive conclusion and could wait until the spring before deciding whether to bring their former academy prospect back.

The club's official statement in June confirmed the existence of a unilateral buy-back option for the 2027-28 season. Crucially, the agreement allowing Paz to remain in Italy for another year was reached at the player's own request, underlining the importance he attaches to regular first-team football at this stage of his career.

The biggest sporting consideration for Madrid remains the presence of Jude Bellingham, whose performances under Mourinho have strengthened his position as the team's principal attacking midfielder.

The England international has scored seven goals and provided five assists in 18 appearances this season, including a goal and an assist in Tuesday's 5-1 victory over PSV. Madrid are also reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new contract for Bellingham, whose existing agreement runs until 2029.

Paz's versatility would give Mourinho some scope to accommodate both players. The Argentine is capable of operating from the right or in a slightly deeper midfield position, although those roles would bring him into direct competition with Arda Guler, Brahim Diaz and Bernardo Silva.

Madrid must also consider how the squad will look next season, with Rodrygo expected to return from injury and Franco Mastantuono due back from his loan spell. Summer signing Yan Diomande represents another significant investment in the attacking department.

Spending £68m on Paz could still make considerable financial sense given his age, development and potential resale value. However, the circumstances that prompted him to remain at Como last summer have hardly changed, particularly with Bellingham enjoying such an influential role under Mourinho.

Waiting until the spring would allow Madrid to assess both Paz's progress and the needs of their own squad before committing to a substantial expenditure. With their final buy-back opportunity approaching, the Spanish giants must determine whether they can offer the Argentine the regular football that has allowed him to flourish in Italy.

#1735. CM: Gimenez could terminate Porto loan early and return to Milan – the situation

Santiago Gimenez left AC Milan in the summer, but he may be returning before the end of his loan deal next summer.

It’s fair to say that Gimenez is one of the most difficult signings to assess from Milan in recent years. On paper, it made plenty of sense why he was right to arrive; he was firing in the Champions League, he had no difficulty scoring in the league and there was the added bonus of him being young and a fan of the club.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With goals against elite teams in Europe too, it made sense why he’d be able to have a successful career at San Siro. Performing on the biggest stage seemingly wasn’t an issue.

So, when he started brightly, fans thought the Rossoneri had struck gold. Yet, that form quickly came undone and Gimenez began to show glimpses, rather than actually developing a portfolio of goalscoring.

After almost being forced out of the club last summer, an injury-ridden campaign effectively ended his time with the Diavolo and he was loaned out in the summer. Yet, he could already be heading back to Italy.

As Calciomercato.com writes, it’s highly unlikely that Porto will activate the €18m buy clause in his deal, and it’s even possible that he doesn’t see out the complete spell of his loan. He’s the third-choice striker, with only four appearances in the Portuguese top flight and one penalty goal; it’s hardly form that warrants making his stay permanent.

Now, ahead of the January mercato, a meeting is planned with Rafaela Pimenta to discuss what would be best for his career. A return to Milanello cannot be ruled out, but it wouldn’t be permanent. He’s not part of Ruben Amorim’s plans, so a new destination would need to be found.

What is for sure, though, is that his value has only dropped further with his Portuguese adventure…

#1734. Liverpool XI vs Everton: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League

Liverpool are full of confidence as they travel to face rivals Everton in the latest Merseyside derby on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola’s surging Reds have been piling up the goals since the November international break - scoring seven times across their last two fixtures alone.

A hugely satisfying 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United at Anfield last weekend in what was Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge of the visitors was quickly followed by a 3-0 victory in the Champions League away at Club Brugge.

Their two statement signings from last summer - Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak - are both hitting top form, which bodes well for this weekend’s derby showdown.

Iraola will likely already know his starting XI for the short trip to Everton, based on the strong form of his team.

Stalwart Alisson will start in goal, while Virgil van Dijk will return to captain the side after being rested in Belgium on Wednesday night.

Ronald Araujo will be shifted to right-back as it is unlikely that Jeremie Frimpong will be asked to play twice in the span of five days following injury.

Jeremy Jacquet will partner Van Dijk in central defence, while Milos Kerkez looks set to make his 90th appearance under Iraola - the left-back having been trusted by his head coach at both Liverpool and Bournemouth.

Dominik Szoboszlai seems to have put his injury woes in the past, and while young Trey Nyoni has impressed when given opportunities this term, Alexis Mac Allister will surely get the nod alongside him in the midfield engine room as Ryan Gravenberch remains a doubt with ongoing heel pain.

The aforementioned Wirtz is playing the best football of his Liverpool career to date; Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola look set to line up either side of the German, with Victor Munoz forced off injured against Brugge to join Cody Gakpo in the treatment room.

#1733. Man City ‘close’ to major injury boost as Enzo Maresca reveals latest team news before Arsenal

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Antoine Semenyo is close to returning for Manchester City, Enzo Maresca has confirmed.

The Ghana international has not featured for Man City since sustaining a knee injury in the 3-2 victory over Ipswich on October 17, missing the last eight games across all competitions as a result.

During this period, City have not won a Premier League game and head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday to face leaders and reigning champions Arsenal.

Semenyo is not expected to be available for the trip to north London, though he could return against either Leeds or Brentford within the next week following a positive update from Maresca.

“We have good news, Antoine is quite close,” Maresca said in Friday’s pre-match press conference. “It’s good news for us. He is already on the pitch - he is very close, hopefully it can be next week, we hope so.

“I was laughing with him yesterday or two days ago. I told him in the Premier League the last game we won was with him on the pitch, so I said we need him back soon to win games.

“Antoine is an important player but we have more players in his position that are doing well like Iliman in this moment. But he needs time to recover.”

Semenyo had been enjoying a decent start to his first full season as a Man City player before being struck down by injury, scoring twice and weighing in with three assists in seven appearances.

The winger also started City’s big away wins over Manchester United and Liverpool, two results that has boosted Maresca’s belief that his side can end their recent slump with victory at Arsenal.

He added: “I think we already showed this season we are able to win important games, to win away. So I don’t see any reason why we are not able to win there.

“We have shown this season we can win important games away. Old Trafford and Anfield are two important away games and Sunday we have another one.

“We showed already and we can win again.”

#1732. Vitoria de Guimaraes vs Estrela Amadora - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 21:01

Vitoria de Guimaraes will look to end a three-match winless run across all competitions when they welcome Estrela Amadora to Estadio D. Afonso Henriques on Saturday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the Primeira Liga table with nine points from 11 matches, just one point and two places behind the visitors, whose early-season resilience has begun to fade.

Vitoria endured their lowest league finish in eight years last term, ending the campaign in ninth place, and their efforts to climb back towards the higher reaches of the table this season have so far proved difficult.

Closer to the relegation zone than the European places, Tiago Margarido's side sit just one point above the relegation playoff spot and 11 behind fifth-placed Arouca, having managed only two wins from their opening 11 league matches (D3, L6).

With victories proving hard to come by, Vitoria have won just one of their eight league games (D3, L4) since beating Nacional on matchday three, with their most recent triumph coming in a 5-0 thrashing of Maritimo on October 23.

Margarido's side have since played out a goalless draw with Gil Vicente before suffering a 2-1 defeat to leaders Porto in their latest top-flight outing, leaving the Guimaraes club with 11 goals scored and 12 conceded in the league this season.

Vitoria suffered another setback at the weekend, when they were eliminated from the Taca de Portugal following a 2-0 defeat to Braga, meaning they have now lost consecutive matches at D. Afonso Henriques for the first time since December 2025.

Meanwhile, the Conquerors have collected eight points from six league matches (W2, D2, L2) at the Minho ground this season and will be looking to improve that tally with a positive result on Saturday.

Estrela, on the other hand, have seen their solid start to the campaign under manager Pepa fade, having now lost each of their last five league matches following an unbeaten run across their opening six fixtures.

While defeats to Academico, Arouca and Casa Pia were disappointing, the Tricolores' two most recent losses have been particularly painful, as they conceded stoppage-time winners in a 2-1 defeat to Moreirense and a 3-2 setback against Benfica.

As a result, Estrela have conceded at least twice in nine of their 11 league matches this season and shipped a total of 22 goals in the Primeira Liga campaign, with only Rio Ave (24) allowing more, while the Amadora club have scored 17 at the other end.

However, there was some encouragement in their most recent outing, as the Tricolores defeated Portimonense 1-0 in the Taca de Portugal to secure a place in the last 16 and record their first clean sheet in 13 matches.

While Estrela will look to build on that cup success, they have a poor away record to contend with heading into the weekend, having managed just one league victory in 14 away games this year (D5, L8).

The visitors have also struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last six league encounters and losing five, including a 2-1 defeat at D. Afonso Henriques in February.

Vitoria de Guimaraes form (all competitions):

Vitoria will be without Toni Borevkovic, who is suspended after collecting his fifth yellow card against Porto, with Thiago Balieiro expected to be the leading candidate to replace him in central defence.

The hosts have also suffered a major setback at left-back, as Joao Mendes has been ruled out for the rest of the season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury to his right knee, while backup Francisco Dias is also unavailable with a right foot sprain.

As a result, Tomas Rodrigues has been called up from the B team to provide cover on the left, although Mohammed Kebdani could feature there, while goalkeeper Juan Castillo has returned to training after an ankle injury but Lucas Furtado is expected to retain his place between the sticks.

Estrela have no reported suspensions, while Jeremy Arevalo is a doubt with a back problem that has prevented him from featuring for the Tricolores since joining from Stuttgart in the summer.

Eddy Doue and Beni Souza have been left out of recent squads for disciplinary reasons and remain doubts for Saturday's trip to Guimaraes.

Leandro Antonetti ended a six-match league goal drought by scoring against Benfica and currently leads the team with five Primeira Liga goals this season, a tally he will be looking to add to this weekend.

Ian Stoica also scored his first goal in seven matches with the winner against Portimonense in the domestic cup and will be keen to find greater consistency in front of goal.

Vitoria de Guimaraes possible starting lineup:

Furtado; Strata, Balieiro, Sidibe, Kebdani; Nogueira, Mukendi; G Silva, Samu, Camara; Jakupovic

Estrela Amadora possible starting lineup:

Linck; Scholze, Schappo, L Patrick, R Soares; Jansson, Serra; Marcus, Zvonarek, Stoica; Antonetti

Neither side has been convincing in recent weeks, but Vitoria's stronger head-to-head record and home advantage could give them the edge against an Estrela team that have lost five consecutive league matches, making a home victory look feasible.

#1731. Chelsea seal exciting midfielder signing after unexpected transfer twist

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally expected to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a pre-agreement contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, said that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their plans after he impressed during Chelsea trials.

Zongo made his senior international debut for Burkina Faso aged just 16 last month, when he came off the bench to play in the second half of a 7-0 friendly defeat by Argentina in Buenos Aires.

The teenager previously impressed when he starred for Burkina Faso on their run to the quarter-finals of the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar last autumn. The midfielder scored the winner as his nation stunned Germany in the round of 16.

Scouts from a number of top European clubs were in attendance at games across the tournament and many took note of the performances produced by Zongo, who was 15 at the time.

Zongo had previously been linked with several other suitors, including LaLiga outfit Villarreal.
