#1730. Transfer news LIVE: Nico Paz to Arsenal twist; Man Utd boost; Chelsea shock; Liverpool, Tottenham done deals

It’s a little over a month now until the opening of the January transfer window, with Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham all trying to line up some statement early signings. Arsenal are believed to be closely tracking Como star Nico Paz but face a battle with Manchester United, having also taken an interest in Carlos Forbs as they ponder moves for the likes of Antonio Nusa and top target Eli Junior Kroupi.

Maxi Araujo is said to be open to joining Manchester United in a huge boost for Mauricio Pochettino, who wants to further strengthen his defence amid pursuits of Calvin Bassey, Jarrad Branthwaite and Nathan Collins. A new striker is also high on the shortlist, though Dominic Calvert-Lewin has agreed a contract extension at Leeds. Chelsea are being linked with a shock Antonio Rudiger reunion as they also push hard to win the crowded race for Alex Scott, having fast-tracked the arrival of wonderkid Mohamed Zongo.

Liverpool have struck a deal for Sidy Barhama Ndiaye and are now rumoured to be eyeing Alejandro Balde, while Tottenham have beaten Arsenal to the signing of ex-West Ham youngster Isaac Allen as they also step up interest in Vangelis Pavlidis and Hakan Calhanoglu. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year, writes Dom Smith.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally due to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, said that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their plans after he impressed during trials.

Manchester United have reportedly activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract.

The influential Red Devils captain was previously set to see his deal at Old Trafford expire in the summer, with speculation that he could depart after previous strong links to Saudi Arabia.

But United always possessed the option to trigger an automatic one-year extension, which they have now done.

Fernandes’ contract is now valid until June 2028, but The Athletic’s David Ornstein reports that such an extension will not necessarily prevent the Portugal playmaker from leaving next summer.

It means that if he does go, then United will at least receive a transfer fee.

Manchester United have a potential ace up their sleeve in transfer talks over Nico Paz.

Argentine star Paz is enjoying a burgeoning reputation across Europe after a remarkable start to the season with Como, which has seen him score six goals from attacking midfield - including two against Man Utd in the Champions League last month.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid in a deal worth around £5million, and it had long been expected that the player would return to the Spanish giants, who hold an €80m (£67m) buy-back clause for Paz.

But The Athletic report that Paz does not currently favour a return to Spain, where he will not be a key player, and is said to be attracted by the prospect of joining Man Utd who need a long-term replacement for captain Bruno Fernandes.

The race for Paz is set to be fierce, but Man Utd will hope they have an advantage over rivals in the form of new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Luka Vuskovic has revealed he chose to leave Tottenham for career stability, admitting that not a single Spurs manager spoke to him during the three years he was on the club’s books.

Spurs wanted Vuskovic to go out on loan again, with De Zerbi unable to offer him a place in the starting lineup, but the youngster was not keen on another season of upheaval and made it clear he wanted a permanent home.

“That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic said in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

“Before they signed everybody, they said they don’t see me at the moment as a starting player.

“Tottenham said they don’t want me at the minute, so I said, ‘OK, I have no problem with that, you gave me a loan already when I was 16, I just want to play somewhere where the club wants me. You can earn from me, so I think it’s fair for both of us.’ ”

Chelsea are being linked with a shock reunion with Antonio Rudiger in January.

The German defender previously spent five years at Stamford Bridge before leaving for Real Madrid in 2022.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea could make a cut-price swoop to bring Rudiger back to west London before his current contract at the Bernabeu expires next summer.

He is struggling for game time under Jose Mourinho, while Xabi Alonso needs to quickly improve a defence that is leaking goals.

It looks like Arsenal will face a major fight from Manchester United over Nico Paz.

As mentioned already this morning, the Gunners are believed to be closely monitoring Como’s rising superstar, along with the likes of Liverpool and Tottenham.

But The Athletic’s David Ornstein now claims that Manchester United will pursue Paz if captain Bruno Fernandes leaves the club this summer, with a switch to Old Trafford said to hold some appeal for the Argentine.

It looks like Paz does not want to return to Real Madrid as things stand currently, despite their €80m buy-back clause.

Manchester United look to have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Maxi Araujo.

The Uruguay and Sporting defender has emerged as a potential candidate to become Mauricio Pochettino’s first Old Trafford signing during the January transfer window as the new manager seeks to improve his options at left-back.

According to Sport Witness, Araujo’s camp are open to the move, which could apparently cost around €50m-€60m despite the €80m release clause in his contract at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Arsenal are interested in a blockbuster deal for Nico Paz, reports claim.

The Argentine playmaker has been central to the stunning rise of Serie A side Como under ex-Gunners star Cesc Fabregas, having left Real Madrid for Italy in 2024.

Los Blancos have a buy-back option for Paz next summer said to be valued at around €80m, though he is also attracting plenty of interest from elsewhere.

CaughtOffside cite reports claiming that Arsenal are closely tracking the 22-year-old, along with Liverpool and Tottenham, with a return to Madrid looking unlikely as things stand.

Richarlison is open to moving to Saudi Arabia to end his Tottenham exile.

The striker has been frozen out at Spurs by manager Roberto De Zerbi after failing to agree a summer exit.

Everton, Vasco da Gama and Trabzonspor were all said to have explored deals for Richarlison, who ended up staying put at Spurs despite being left out of De Zerbi's Premier League squad.

Manchester United fans will be dismayed by reports that Mauricio Pochettino will have just £50million to improve his squad during the January transfer window.

A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

The second window of the season often leads to inflated prices, with clubs capitalising upon other teams’ struggles and desperate need for new players.

#1728. SC Paderborn vs Schalke 04 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 21:10, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 23:58

SC Paderborn's clash with visitors Schalke 04 on Saturday at Home Deluxe Arena will be crucial in the Bundesliga's relegation battle.

Sitting 15th with 10 points, the hosts are only above 16th-placed Schalke by three points, and a defeat could leave them as low as 17th by the end of matchweek 11.

The relegation battle looks set to be intense, as while last-placed Borussia Monchengladbach are stranded in 18th, only three points separate 17th from 13th.

Paderborn are one place above the league's relegation playoff spot following their 4-0 loss against Bayer Leverkusen on November 21.

That was their first defeat in five Bundesliga games, though the club drew three times in that period, with their only triumph a 1-0 win against Hamburger SV on October 24.

The hosts have failed to score in three of their last four games in all competitions, and they conceded as many goals in their past two clashes (six) as they had in their prior six contests.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will be pleased by his side's home record given they have won two of their five top-flight fixtures at Home Deluxe Arena while only being beaten twice.

Schalke could view their goalless stalemate with Stuttgart on November 21 positively, especially as it arrested a four-match losing streak.

However, it would be understandable if boss Miron Muslic was feeling pressure given he has failed to oversee a victory in eight games, with his side losing on five occasions.

The visitors might take comfort from the fact they have beaten their hosts in their two most recent meetings, the latest of which was a 3-2 success in the 2. Bundesliga in April 2026.

Die Knappen rank 18th in the division for goals scored (five), though only Borussia Dortmund (seven), Bayern Munich (10) and Freiburg (10) have conceded fewer times (11).

Schalke's form on the road has been poor considering they are winless in their last four away outings, suffering three losses.

Paderborn will be unable to call upon defenders Marcel Hoffmeier (muscle) and Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant (ankle), as well as forward Timur Gayret (knee).

Jano ter Horst, Tjark Scheller and Mattes Hansen have been regulars in the backline, and they are set to protect goalkeeper Nahuel Noll.

Stefano Marino and Marvin Pieringer are likely to be trusted as a front two, and they will be keen to improve upon their tallies of two and one league goal respectively.

Schalke's absentee list is extensive, with defender Timo Becker, midfielder Ron Schallenberg and forward Emil Hojlund three of seven injured stars.

Vitalie Becker will start in the backline, Soufian El-Faouzi is likely to anchor the middle of the pitch and Moussa Sylla is certain to lead the frontline.

Noll; Ter Horst, Scheller, Hansen; Curda, Baack, Castaneda, Vidovic, Obermair; Marino, Pieringer

Karius; Ebimbe, Katic, Kurucay, Becker; El-Faouzi, Ljubicic; Hwang, Karaman, Aouchiche; Sylla

While both teams have significantly struggled for results lately, it is impossible for both teams to lose on Saturday.

Perhaps the most likely outcome is a stalemate, especially as neither have proven to be particularly productive in the final third.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali has returned to training ahead of Tottenham’s visit to Sunderland, but Savio is expected to spend a significant period on the sidelines after suffering the recurrence of a hamstring injury.

Tonali missed Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last weekend due to illness, but is set to be available for selection when Roberto De Zerbi’s side travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

Savio, meanwhile, was named on the bench against Ipswich, having missed the previous four games. The 22-year-old was introduced in the second half, but lasted just 26 minutes before he had to come off injured.

Savio was visibly upset as he headed down the tunnel, and De Zerbi confirmed at his pre-Sunderland press conference on Friday that the Brazilian would miss the festive period.

Asked if Savio may not play again this year, De Zerbi said: “Yeah, I think [he will miss the Christmas period].

“Unfortunately it’s a tough situation to accept. He’s a new guy and he’s suffering with these new injuries. But this is football, if you see other European clubs they’re all suffering these injuries.”

De Zerbi added: “Now he needs time. He needs hard work with the medical staff. Then in 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don’t know, when he comes back, he will be crucial for us in the last step of the season.”

Savio joins fellow Tottenham wingers Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk on the sidelines, meaning teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut against Ipswich before being handed a new contract, could be in line for more minutes.

Fears over an injury to Omar Marmoush remain despite the forward appearing in training footage posted across Spurs’ social media channels on Thursday. The Egyptian was this week subject of online speculation that he required assessment over a possible knee problem.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo remains a doubt despite returning to training following a calf injury, while Lucas Bergvall will be assessed having suffered from illness this week.

Long-term absentees Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are both getting closer to a return to action, but neither player is expected to be challenging for minutes in the coming weeks.

#1726. The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH

Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026

The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian said, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

What the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed new 100,000 stadium

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed new 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

It cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 21:14

Separated by just two points around the top eight of the Championship table, Queens Park Rangers and Sheffield United will square off at MATRADE Loftus Road on Saturday.

The hosts sit seventh having extended an unbeaten streak with an away draw in midweek, while their visitors sit a point off the playoff spots after a win and a draw of their own since the international break.

Queens Park Rangers return to MATRADE Loftus Road on Saturday with the hopes of extending an unbeaten run in the Championship and strengthening their position in the top eight.

In their second season under Julien Stephan, following a 15th-placed finish last time around, they currently find themselves seventh having earned 28 points from their first 17 outings, winning seven and only losing three of those with only league leaders Middlesbrough suffering fewer defeats.

The Hoops' success has largely come at the back, with only three teams conceding fewer than the 19 goals they have allowed, four of which came in an away defeat to Southampton at the end of October.

Stephan's men bounced back and headed into the November international break on the back of a draw against Burnley and a win over Lincoln City, before returning with a 1-0 away victory at Millwall at the weekend and a 1-1 draw against in-form Norwich City at Carrow Road on Tuesday having led through Harvey Vale.

With confidence to take from their return from the recent break, but just two points ahead of their visitors in the battle for playoff places, QPR will bid to make it five games unbeaten and bounce back to winning ways on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to the capital aiming to break into the playoff spots having also enjoyed a positive return from the international break.

After a slow start to their third straight Championship campaign, in which they set out to battle for promotion, Sheffield United seemingly hit their stride after the September and October international break, moving onto 22 points from 14 games with four wins and just one loss in a six-game span.

They would then go into the second break of the term on the back of a disappointing loss away at strugglers Charlton Athletic but bounced back in style on their return last weekend, hosting Watford and dishing out a 4-0 beating as Ben Brereton Diaz had them two up with an early brace and Jordan Ayew and Sydie Peck added second-half goals.

Southampton then visited Bramall Lane on Tuesday, and Chris Wilder's men looked to fall short to a solitary Lewis Dobbin goal, but they were eventually able to level and take a share of the spoils as Peck equalised in the 90th minute.

Now poised to crack the playoff spots with some momentum behind them, having earned 17 points in their last nine matches, Sheffield United sit just one point outside the top eight and two off Saturday's hosts, and they will hope to leapfrog QPR with another victory at the weekend.

QPR remain without defender Amadou Mbengue, who is sidelined with a long-term injury, while Jimmy Dunne should also miss out again having been absent for their last two games.

In Dunne's absence, Jake Clarke-Salter and Ronnie Edwards should partner up at the heart of a back four, while Nicolas Madsen also missed the trip to Norwich meaning Glen Kamara and Jonathan Varane will likely continue their midfield pairing.

Richard Kone and Rumarn Burrell will compete to lead the line, while Ilias Chair will hope to return from the outset in support after Kwame Poku, Harvey Vale and Koki Saito were preferred behind Burrell in midweek.

Sheffield United defender Femi Seriki is ruled out for the season through injury, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One, Joe Rothwell and Jamie Shackleton will likely remain sidelined.

They have two players returning, though, with Japhet Tanganga back available after suspension and the captain set to rejoin Liam Kitching at centre-back, and Ben Brereton Diaz back in contention for an attacking spot after being ineligible to play against parent club Southampton in midweek.

He could take the place of Jordan Ayew, who may be rested after being withdrawn as a precaution on Tuesday following two impressive displays, with Tyrese Campbell and Patrick Bamford also pushing to come in up top, while Kalvin Phillips will hope to return to the starting XI in midfield alongside Sydie Peck.

Charles; Adamson, Clarke-Salter, Edwards, Cirkin; Varane, Kamara; Chair, Vale, Saito; Kone

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Chong, Peck, Phillips, Donovan; Brereton Diaz, Bamford

Both teams head into the weekend with confidence for what should be high quality and evenly-matched encounter.

Sheffield United have certainly improved since their disappointing start to the season, other than the loss to Charlton before the break, and we see them leaving MATRADE Loftus Road with a share of the points.

#1723. Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

There has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

However, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is said to be one of the most serious of the 115.

The damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

The Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

City have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are said to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

City rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for new players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

On Friday, a City spokesman said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and announced in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

City denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

It did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, said: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

“Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”

Ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, said the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, said he believed the club were innocent.

“For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder said while on international duty.

“When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, said: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of New York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 said that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

All the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

As well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

We also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

City have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they said that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also said: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”

Of the Football Leaks documents, City said: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”

#1722. Jarrod Bowen interview: I will discuss West Ham future if Premier League promotion bid fails

Jarrod Bowen has admitted that talks over his West Ham future will take place if a return to the Premier League is not secured this season.

The West Ham captain, who played his 300th game for the club this week, was the subject of Premier League interest at the end of last season following the club’s relegation to the second division for the first time in 14 years, but never considered leaving.

Bowen instead committed his immediate future to West Ham by signing a new contract, which included revised terms to help the club in their bid for promotion.

The 29-year-old says it was an easy decision to stay, but conversations will need to be had if West Ham are resigned to a second season in the second tier.

You don't want to be stuck, you want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away

The Hammers have endured a tricky start to life in the Championship, and currently sit outside the play-off places and winless in four games under new manager Scott Parker.

“I never wanted to leave after being relegated,” Bowen tells Standard Sport.

“I always wanted to give it an opportunity, to go we can get this club back into the Premier League. I wanted to be the spearhead of that.

“I think it's wrong to look too far ahead into the future because I think your energy has to be into this season. But if it doesn't happen, then we will sit down and have a conversation at the end of the season.

“But I think for now, we have to put all our energy into this season because there's something special that we can achieve.”

West Ham have struggled to adapt to the Championship, winning six of their opening 17 games, but Bowen says this came as no surprise to him and believes promotion expert Parker can turn things around.

“He's been brilliant,” Bowen says of former Hammers midfielder Parker, who has earned promotion from the Championship on three seperate occasions. “Someone who understands the club, played so many years here, captained here at this club as well. “We feel we're in a weirdly good place, and we're looking forward to what we've got coming up.”

An edgy 1-0 victory at Swansea last month felt at the time like the making of West Ham as promotion candidates, but they are yet to taste victory since Parker replaced Nuno Espirito Santo in the dugout last month.

The 1-0 defeat to Portsmouth this week prompted Parker to warn that West Ham risk getting stuck in the Championship if they do not adapt to the physical demands of the league.

And Bowen insists promotion back to the top flight is not as easy as some make out.

“Of course you don't want to be stuck,” he continued. “You want to bounce back and be in the Premier League straight away, of course you do.

“But like I said, it's not as easy as what people think or just to expect. Just because you've come down, it'll be easy for you to get back promoted because that's not the case, and we're finding that out right now.”

Bowen was speaking to Standard Sport at the EFL’s Power of 72 event at the London Stadium, promoting West Ham’s Thrive employability programme, which concentrates on providing support to Neet (not in education, employment or training) and underemployed young people in Newham and east London.

EFL Power of 72 celebrates the positive impact EFL Clubs have on their communities and the bond between clubs and local people, with one million people participating in EFL club charity programmes every season.

“It's so important to me because it's something that I've been involved in for a few years now since I've been here,” Bowen said of the Thrive employability programme.

“We have people with different backgrounds, different upbringings, that all have limited opportunities to go out and showcase that. So, the work we're doing is giving them the opportunity to go and showcase what they want to do, giving them the work experience to go on and achieve what they set out to do.”

#1721. Arouca vs Rio Ave - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 26 Nov 2026 21:27, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:00

Still licking their wounds after their Taca de Portugal fourth-round exits, Arouca and Rio Ave return to action in the Portuguese Primeira Liga when they go head to head at the Estadio Municipal de Arouca on Saturday afternoon.

Rio Ave head coach Vasco Seabra will be out to haunt his former employers in his first return to the Municipal since switching teams in October after two years and 68 games in charge of the Arouquenses.

While Vitor Severino’s appointment has restored confidence in Arouca, consecutive defeats in their most recent two outings have raised fresh concerns, particularly after losing 2-1 to third-tier CD Mafra in the Taca de Portugal last Saturday.

The tie took a difficult turn for the Arouquenses when Moussa Camara and Leandro Alves put Mafra two goals up at the Estadio Municipal de Mafra, and while Ivan Barbero pulled one back in the 59th minute to spark a potential comeback, the hosts held on to see out the victory.

This followed a 1-0 defeat against Famalicao at the Estadio Municipal de Famalicao on November 6, when Paulo Moreira netted in the sixth minute of stoppage time to end Arouca’s run of three consecutive victories in the Primeira Liga.

Despite their recent slump, the Porto outfit can take pride in what had been a solid start to the campaign, as they sit fifth in the Primeira Liga standings with 20 points from 11 matches, four points behind the Champions League qualifying places.

A disciplined defence has been key to Arouca’s promising start, as they boast the joint-highest number of clean sheets in the Primeira Liga while conceding just eight goals so far - only league leaders Porto (5) have allowed fewer.

Like the home side, Rio Ave saw their Taca de Portugal journey come to an end at the hands of a lower-tier side last weekend as they fell to a 1-0 loss against Liga 3 outfit SC Vianense on Sunday.

The visitors were guilty of a toothless display in attack at the Estadio Dr. Jose de Matos, with Moises Conceicao’s 33rd-minute strike proving decisive in sending Vianense through to the cup round of 16.

This was in keeping with their struggles in the Primeira Liga, where Rio Ave are on a three-game losing streak, suffering defeats against Famalicao, Academico Viseu and Braga, while managing just four points from eight games since August 28.

Off the back of a 12th-placed finish last season, Vasco Seabra’s men have found the going considerably tougher this time around and are one of the early contenders to go down, having collected just seven points from 11 games to sit 17th in the Primeira Liga table.

With the festive period approaching, Rio Ave will head into the weekend keen to kickstart a turnaround, and they will draw encouragement from recent results against Arouca, having picked up five wins and four draws from the last 11 meetings between the two teams since August 2021.

Arouca will take to the pitch without Spanish forward Miguel Puche, who continues his lengthy spell on the sidelines since sustaining a knee injury in April’s matchup against Estrela Amadora.

Barring any late fitness issues, Puche should be the only absentee for the Arouquenses, giving Severino the luxury of a relatively full strength squad to select from this weekend.

As for Rio Ave, goalkeeper Cezary Miszta remains sidelined with a back injury, while defender Nelson Abbey is also expected to sit out the trip to the Estadio Municipal de Arouca.

Brandon Aguilera, Pedro Amaral and Ze Carlos are all listed as injury doubts, leaving head coach Vasco Seabra with a few selection decisions to make ahead of Saturday's encounter.

#1720. Mikel Arteta hoping Man City charges saga doesn’t overshadow Arsenal clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has urged his Arsenal players to block out all talk of Manchester City’s Premier League charges and ensure they win the title on the pitch.

In September, City were were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, while an independent commission also ruled that the club failed to co-operate with an investigation.

An appeal has been submitted by City, who deny any wrongdoing, and it remains to be seen when a final resolution in the case will be reached.

It is a shadow hanging over the league ahead of Arsenal’s showdown with City in north London on Sunday.

Victory would move the Gunners nine points ahead of Enzo Maresca’s side and leave them in strong shape to defend their league title, regardless of any potential sanctions imposed on City.

Arteta is clear that his players cannot afford any distractions, demanding that they get the job done and defend their crown without relying on a potential points deduction for City.

“That’s the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on,” Arteta said. “There’s nothing else.”

Arsenal were defeated twice by City in the space of three weeks towards the end of last season, first in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley and then in a Premier League clash at the Etihad Stadium. Despite losing the latter game, Arsenal went on to win the title for the first time in 22 years.

A rivalry has built between the two clubs over the past five seasons, having gone toe-to-toe in several title races.

Asked if the guilty verdict against City and the wait for possible sanctions had diminished the significance of Sunday’s meeting, Arteta said: “I hope that it doesn’t because it’s a process that is still open.

“It’s not resolved and we don’t know what is going to happen. So, no, I think when we have two teams at the level that both teams are at right now with the quality players that are on that pitch, it’s a massive game and a big game to enjoy.”

However, when it was put to him that the atmosphere might be particularly emotional due to the strength of feeling from the Arsenal fans, Arteta sidestepped the topic.

“I don’t know,” he said. “That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there.”

#1719. GdS: Unbeaten and hope or room for error – Milan begin Europa League calculations

AC Milan have four games left to play in the Europa League and they’re in the do-or-die stage of the competition already.

Thoughts on the Europa League this season were mixed. On paper, Milan should have been competing at the top. Yet, they’ve struggled through the League Phase so far, leaving themselves with something of a mountain to climb, starting against Olympiacos later this week.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are in a more-than-difficult position. Sitting 28th in the rankings, they are currently outside the qualification spots and calculations are difficult to make about how much they’ll need to improve.

From the past two seasons, they’ll need between 14 and 16 points to qualify for the top eight, which feels like a distant hope. If they’re to achieve that amount, they must win all four of their remaining games and hope that 15 is enough.

The play-offs, on the other hand, are more than feasible. Sitting four places off currently, there’s a one-point gap to overturn and history says they’ll need either nine or 10 points. This would allow far more room for error, with only two wins and a draw needed to ‘guarantee’ a spot in the next round.

In Greece, they’ll face the first hurdle and getting three points would make life much easier for everyone involved.

#1718. Liverpool suspension risks: Key duo walking Premier League tightrope before Chelsea clash

Liverpool are looking up as the hectic period of the campaign approaches.

Andoni Iraola's side have bounced back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce prior to the November international break, and go into the Everton game seeking a fourth straight win across all competitions.

While Sunday’s showdown at the Hill Dickinson Stadium will represent Iraola’s first taste of a Merseyside derby, history largely favours the Reds having lost just one of the last 10 meetings.

It remains to be seen if Victor Munoz is able to shake off a knock and prove his fitness, but two key Liverpool players will have to be careful if selected due to the looming threat of a ban.

With that in mind, here’s a look at the Liverpool players at risk of suspension.

As every club have already been made fully aware of this season, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Liverpool's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Coventry on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

Alexis Mac Allister and summer signing Bradley Barcola are the big suspensions concern for Liverpool at present.

The Argentina international was booked in the win over Crystal Palace so had to watch his step in the 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United, but Barcola is a new suspension risk after being cautioned in the second half last weekend.

As such, if the Frenchman and/or Mac Allister are shown a yellow card in the Merseyside derby, a one-match ban must be served in the very next fixture - at home to Sunderland on December 2.

Ultimately, the pair are walking the disciplinary tightrope for upcoming games against Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds, Tottenham, Hull, Aston Villa and Coventry.

Furthermore, with Liverpool taking on Chelsea next weekend, Barcola and/or Mac Allister would be suspended for the trip to Stamford Bridge if either are booked against the Black Cats.

Ronald Araujo, Milos Kerkez and Virgil van Dijk are on three yellow cards, while Jeremy Jacquet and Munoz are among a host of Liverpool players still in danger of being suspended.

#1717. Wycombe Wanderers vs Bradford City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 21:41

After returning to the top six of the League One table with a midweek victory, Bradford City will head to Adams Park to take on Wycombe Wanderers on Saturday.

The visitors sit sixth and within touching distance of the top two, while their hosts find themselves 15th on the back of a loss and a draw.

Wycombe Wanderers return to action at Adams Park on Saturday with the hopes of kickstarting a climb up the League One table in the midst of a disappointing run.

They spent the first five games of 2026-27 under Michael Duff, who now leads the visitors, going winless before he was replaced by Tom Hounsell who oversaw an upturn in form.

The Chairboys won three, drew one and lost one of their first five league outings under the new boss but have since put one more notch in the wins column in five further third-tier matches.

That came at home to Burton Albion alongside an FA Cup victory, before Hounsell's men lost a dramatic game to Oxford United last weekend, having led 3-0 through Jayden Wareham, Malik Mothersille and Aaron Morley and been reduced to 10 men with Dan Casey and Luke Leahy sent off before the hosts scored four goals in the final 20 minutes to snatch all three points.

Left wounded by that result, and now on the back of a midweek 1-1 draw with strugglers Bromley, Wycombe Wanderers find themselves 15th and will be keen to put another positive run together beginning with a home win at the weekend.

They meet a former boss who arrives at Adams Park in search of back-to-back victories as Bradford City manager to strengthen their standing in the playoff places.

Braford City's 2026-27 has also been a mixed one thus far, having built on their 2024-25 promotion and 2025-26 playoff loss in League One with a fast start under Graham Alexander, who departed in September, leaving them on 15 points from seven games.

Duff has since taken charge and overseen seven league matches, with the Bantams winning two, drawing four and losing one of those while keeping five clean sheets to move onto a league-high tally of 10 for the season in 15 League One matches.

Following consecutive dominant cup victories, winning 7-0 and 4-0, and a 2-2 draw against Doncaster Rovers, the Bantams headed into a second straight Yorkshire Derby on Tuesday at home to Barnsley and dished out a 3-0 beating as Stephen Humphrys scored a brace and Jake Beesley added a late third from the spot.

Now back in the top six after a blip in the early stages under Duff, while boasting the league's best defensive record and having scored 16 goals in their last four matches to begin to remedy their attacking struggles, Bradford City will bid to make it consecutive wins on Saturday to close in on the automatic promotion spots.

Wycombe Wanderers form (all competitions):

Wycombe Wanderers will remain without Armando Quitirna, Ewan Henderson and Danny Ings through injuries.

Dan Casey and Luke Leahy are back in contention after suspensions for their red cards against Oxford, though, and Casey should rejoin Connor Taylor at the back.

Wareham will continue to lead the line, having scored eight goals in 11 league appearances so far this season, while Caolan Boyd-Munce could again join Cauley Woodrow and Malik Mothersille in support with Fred Onyedinma having missed the last three matches.

Bradford City will field a similar starting XI from the 3-0 midweek win over Barnsley, with Bobby Pointon, Tyreik Wright and George Lapslie sidelined by injuries and key midfielder Antoni Sarcevic also set to miss out again.

They are without Ibou Touray, though, as he is suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards, and he may be replaced by Corey O'Keeffe or Josh Neufville, who has returned in the last two games after an injury layoff.

Macaulay Gillesphey got the nod over George Pratt in midweek at the back and should again join Aden Baldwin and Matthew Pennington, while Humphrys will lead the line after Tuesday's brace and Beesley and Nick Powell will battle to come in in place of Will Swan and Adam Phillips.

Wycombe Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Bradford City are showing signs of returning to their best after a slow start under Duff, particularly improving their attacking output in recent weeks while maintaining League One's best defensive record, and we back them to come out on top against a Wycombe side lacking momentum.

#1716. Manchester United have new suspension risk after Leny Yoro red card appeal

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for selection against Brentford this weekend, though a fellow defender remains at risk of a Premier League suspension.

Yoro was dismissed after just eight minutes in Man United’s defeat to Liverpool last Sunday, as Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after succeeding Michael Carrick as head coach quickly turned into a nightmare.

The Frenchman was given his marching orders for bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box, with the Premier League revealing the red card was shown to the United defender “for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO)”.

However, Man Utd appealed the decision and it has proven successful with Yoro cleared to face Brentford on Saturday.

A statement from the FA read: “Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.”

Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a claim of wrongful dismissal

United have had to deal with their fair share of suspensions already this season. Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matheus Cunha and, more recently, Youri Tielemans, have all been sent-off at some point to raise concerns over a disciplinary issue within the squad.

A further suspension concern is in the form of central defender Harry Maguire, who is currently on four Premier League yellow cards.

As per the rules, players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

Man United's cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the away game against Brighton on January 2, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

#1714. Angers vs Lens - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 26 Nov 2026 22:39, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 09:56

Relegation-zone Angers SCO host RC Lens in Ligue 1 on Saturday at Stade Raymond Kopa.

The home side sit 17th in the the Ligue 1 table with eight points after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Paris FC, while 11th-placed Sang et Or, on 14 points, are playing under their third head coach of the season.

Les Scoistes have won two of their 11 league games under Stephane Gilli, who replaced Alexandre Dujeux on June 9 after Dujeux resigned and moved to Lorient.

Their last six league results read lost, lost, drawn, lost, lost, lost, a stretch in which Angers have scored three goals and conceded 18.

Angers held Paris FC goalless for the first 46 minutes on Sunday, then conceded four second-half goals, two of them within 10 minutes of the restart.

Gilli returned to Stade Jean Bouin as a former Paris FC head coach, and his plan to smother their short passing worked only until Patrick Zabi opened the scoring in the 47th minute.

Amine El Ouazzani and Prosper Peter lead the club with two league goals each, but only nine have been scored in 11 games.

Angers have collected four points from six home league games, winning once and drawing once, with a 0-0 draw against Lorient on October 25 the highlight.

Gilli said after the 2-0 home defeat to Nice on November 8 that he felt he was repeating the same message after every match.

Angers have lost each of their last six Ligue 1 meetings with Lens, including a 5-1 defeat at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on March 20 in which Lanroy Machine scored their only goal.

Les Sang et Or turned to Didier Digard on November 13, three days after sacking interim head coach Yannick Cahuzac, who had replaced Dino Toppmoller on September 15.

Cahuzac lost his job six days after a 9-1 home defeat to Como in the Champions League, a result that still hangs over the squad.

Digard’s first game ended in a 1-1 home draw with Toulouse on November 21, Michael Cuisance equalising from a Florian Thauvin assist, and his first away trip brought a 3-1 defeat at RB Leipzig on Tuesday.

Lens have won four, drawn two and lost five of their 11 league games, scoring 18 and conceding 16, and they have not kept a single clean sheet.

Their 35 goals conceded in all competitions, 16 in the league and 19 in the Champions League, is the second-worst total among clubs in Europe’s five major leagues, behind Manchester United's 36.

Their away league record reads one win, one draw and three defeats, the win being a 3-1 victory at Troyes on October 17.

Lens are winless in five games in all competitions, with the last victory a 2-1 home win over Paris FC on October 24.

Thauvin, 33, has five goals and eight assists in the league, and he scored twice in Lens’ 2-1 win at Angers on November 30, 2025.

Opta data showed after Leipzig that Thauvin has lost 15 of his 17 Champions League appearances, and Lens are 33rd in the league phase with three points from five games.

On a brighter note, Lens have won their last three visits to Stade Raymond Kopa, by 2-1 in November 2022, 1-0 in August 2024 and 2-1 last season.

Gilli had only two absentees at Wednesday’s training session, goalkeeper Melvin Zinga with a shoulder problem and midfielder Bane Diatta with an ankle injury, while Joseph Kalulu was back after cutting short Tuesday’s session.

Jordan Lefort should return after a one-match suspension, and El Ouazzani is available again after missing two games, which could push Usman Simbakoli, who made his first start of the season at Paris FC, back to the bench.

For the visitors, Ruben Aguilar, hurt against Toulouse, is out alongside Odsonne Edouard, who has had adductor surgery, and Maik Nawrocki, who has a ruptured cruciate ligament.

Cuisance missed the Leipzig game through illness and remains a doubt, while Abdallah Sima, back from a thigh injury, and Ismaelo Ganiou, back from meniscus surgery, are available again.

Lopes; Arcus, Camara, Lefort, Kalulu; Belkebla, Van den Boomen; Belkhdim, Sbai, El Ouazzani; Peter

Risser; Todibo, Baidoo, Ganiou; Abdulhamid, Haidara, Titraoui, Udol; Thauvin, Hazard; Sima

Lens have conceded in all 11 league games this season, so Angers, with El Ouazzani back from injury, should find at least one chance against a defence that has let in 35 goals across all competitions.

Angers have scored only two goals in their last five league games, failing to score in four of them, which is why the hosts are unlikely to take more than one.

The visitors’ away record of one win in five is a genuine concern, but a first league win since October 24 looks the most likely outcome.

#1712. Will Man City be stripped of Premier League titles? Possible sanctions amid new update before Arsenal showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal take on Manchester City in the standout Premier League fixture this weekend, though it will be played in the backdrop of uncertainty.

While it is first against third and a showdown between last season’s top two, the outcome at the Emirates Stadium may not have too much of an impact on this year’s title race.

This is because Man City head to north London on the back of being handed an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges.

Back in October, City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City, however, have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should Man City’s appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.

Meanwhile, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport that Man City’s owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for its breaking financial rules.

Below is a breakdown of what sanctions Man City could potentially face if their appeal is unsuccessful.

Expulsion from the Premier League: The most severe sanction could see Man City removed from the Premier League and relegated to the Championship, with any decision subject to the relevant league rules and the outcome of any appeal.

Suspension from Premier League matches: Another potential sanction would be a suspension. The club could potentially be suspended from participating in Premier League fixtures for a specified period.

More London travel chaos as weekend Tube and rail closures follow end of strike

Man Utd defender at risk of suspension after Leny Yoro red card appeal

Liverpool handed new suspension risk ahead of Chelsea clash

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Points deduction: A significant deduction in points could be imposed, either during the current season or in a future campaign.

The size and timing of any deduction would be determined as part of the sanctions process.

Stripping of titles and trophies: Retrospective sporting penalties could also potentially affect honours that were won during the period covered by the charges.

In this scenario, Arsenal would not be awarded a single retrospective Premier League title. This is because the seasons in which they finished runners-up to Man City has not been under investigation. The Gunners would, though get a League Cup after being demolished 3-0 by City in the 2017-18 final at Wembley.

However, no decision has been made to strip City of any titles or trophies.

Transfer restrictions: The club could potentially face restrictions on registering or signing players for one or more transfer windows.

Fines: City could also face substantial financial penalties. The club could be ordered to pay fines, compensation or costs associated with the proceedings.

The sanctions process is separate from the commission’s determination on the charges, meaning City’s punishment remains to be decided.

#1711. Scotland’s Pocognoli era starts with encouraging signs but familiar issues in front of goal

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant said: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

“They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a big game again on Tuesday so it’s important to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

“We’ve had a great week. A new manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

“I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”

Pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

Scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

Oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

How has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

Another change is here for Scotland, with Gannon-Doak on to replace Hickey.

Another big chance for Scotland. This time Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie goes close.Slovenia 0-0 Scotland - watch the closing stages on BBC One. pic.twitter.com/xMe5gRNgEr

From the resulting corner, Oblak is there again to thwart McBurnie’s point-blank header. The referee then blows his whistle to relieve the pressure on Slovenia. Somehow, the scoreline remains goalless.

The hosts make another double change as Sporar and Brekalo depart for Vipotnik and Balkovec.

Welsh spots Bowie’s run and threads a perfectly-weighted pass through to the forward. From an unfavourable angle, the substitute’s one-on-one attempt is blocked by Oblak.

Another massive chance for Scotland! McGinn’s searching corner is met by Hickey, who flicks a header wide of the far post. Scotland’s second-half performance deserves a goal.

Pocognoli orders Scotland’s first alteration of the game, with Bowie replacing Ure up top.

Hickey finds himself very high up the pitch and tries to tee up Ure with a cushioned header, but there isn’t enough power on the pass.

Gilmour and Ure link up effectively on the counter, but the latter’s pull-back is intercepted by Drkusic.

Slovenia then make two changes as Zabukovnik and Zec replace Elsnik and Drkusic.

McGinn strides forward and tries to find Ure, but Slovenia rush back to scramble it clear. Scotland are really pushing for the opening goal.

Gilmour and McBurnie play a devastating one-two, allowing the midfielder to advance into the penalty area. He shoots and aims for the far corner, but his placed effort is collected impressively by Oblak, who makes another crucial intervention.

The second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

McBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

McBurnie latches onto a loose ball and skips away from Drkusic’s sliding challenge. One-on-one, the striker tries to round Oblak, but the Slovenian goalkeeper does sensationally to apprehend him. Upon reflection, it looks like McBurnie should have just shot and tried to put the ball between Oblak’s legs. He did the hard part, but lacked a clinical finish.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb

McGinn brilliantly turns Drkusic on the halfway line and then tees up Gilmour. The Napoli midfielder tries to float a pass over to the onrushing Robertson, but he hits the switch of play straight out for a throw-in. In defence of Gilmour, the pitch really doesn’t look in the best condition, with various players struggling regarding their weight of pass.

We are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a new system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

Despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

HALF TIME: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland.No goals at the break in Ljubljana.#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/6VGFRprBiz

Ure strikes the woodwork! The Sevilla striker is agonisingly close to a debut goal for his country. He cuts inside to work some space and fires a low effort at goal, but his shot hits the post.

Scotland's best chance of the game so far 😯 Sevilla striker and debutant Robbie Ure strikes the post just before half-time.However, it remains goalless at the break.📺 Watch Slovenia v Scotland on BBC One 🇸🇮 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 pic.twitter.com/fm1wH2fOej

Much better from Scotland! McGinn turns his marker and clips a wonderful pass over to Ure, who has drifted out wide. The ball is then delivered into the box toward McGinn, whose header bounces off McBurnie. Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

Robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

It’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

Similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

Since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

The hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

Matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

Slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is launched forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

Slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

The hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

New Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli sings Flower of Scotland as he takes charge of the national side for the first time 🎶 🇸🇮 Slovenia v Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 is live on BBC One now.#BBCFootball #NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/I2aeqYkNGB

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off, here’s a reminder of both teams’ line-ups.

Slovenia: Oblak, Brekalo, Bijol, Drkusic, Janza, Karnicnik, Cerin, Elsnik, Matko, Sturm, Sporar.

"Let's go!" 👏#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/HBvPJdFkFb

Luis Binks of Brondby, as well as Colby Donovan and Josh McPake, who play for Celtic and Hearts respectively, are all amongst the substitutes. This hopeful trio are all in line for their Scotland debuts if they enter the action later this afternoon.

Slovenski navijači se že zbirajo 👊🇸🇮#SrceBije 🇸🇮 pic.twitter.com/dM9UArGgl3

How much do the Tartan Army really know about new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli? 🤔 We sent Jonathan Sutherland around Ljubljana to find out.📺 Watch 🇸🇮 Slovenia v Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 on Saturday on BBC One from 13:45 BST. pic.twitter.com/KSurjSmKwL

'We're not going to be perfect right away but we still demand results'Scotland's Lewis Ferguson as the team begins a new era under Sebastien Pocognoli 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿#BBCFootball pic.twitter.com/42WCJh66gc
